544413|2026-09.headline: Digitide Q2 FY27 revenue fell 2% QoQ to INR 760 crore, but EBITDA rose 2.5% to INR 79 crore (10.4% margin) and TCV nearly doubled to ~INR 400 crore.
544413|2026-09.overview: Revenue was about INR 760 crore, down 2% sequentially, as management deliberately exited low-return work and repriced contracts. EBITDA rose 2.5% QoQ to about INR 79 crore, with margin up 45 bps to 10.4%, and reported PAT rose to INR 8.9 crore from INR 2.9 crore in Q1 with no exceptional items. Sales momentum improved: TCV rose 95% QoQ to nearly INR 400 crore and AI-led revenue doubled to INR 30.5 crore. Management reiterated a 200 bps full-year EBITDA margin improvement target but gave no numerical revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: up from INR 2.9 crore in Q1 (tripled)
vs INR 12 crore in Q2 FY26

segments.name: India BPM
segments.commentary: Margin slightly declined to 13.6%; management cited wage revisions, repricing of existing contracts and exits of low-return work. India BPO is about 50-52% of wallet share.

segments.name: Tech & digital
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 244 crore, +6.6% YoY; segment margin rose 315 bps to 11.1%. Platforms are expected to earn 2-3x BPO profitability per management.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 323 crore, +13.5% YoY, 42.5% of revenue. International BPO is about 6-7% of wallet share.

segments.name: GCC / BOT
segments.commentary: Signed a BOT mandate to hire 1,000 people in the Philippines; about 700 already mobilised. Five GCC implementations in total, four managed-services.

segments.name: AI revenue
segments.commentary: INR 30.5 crore, split roughly 35-37% AI BPM, 30-35% platforms, 27-28% professional services; 4.1% of revenue vs 1.9% in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 target of 200 bps EBITDA margin improvement reiterated; management said it is a tough challenge and 45 bps QoQ was already delivered.
Management expects an exit-year EBITDA margin around 13%, which an analyst asked about; management said it remains committed but did not restate the figure explicitly.
Cost-structure actions are expected to be visible in H2 FY27; DSO expected to improve in H2.
TCV conversion rule of thumb: 30-35% of FY27 TCV expected to convert to revenue this fiscal; platforms take 10-16 weeks from booking to realisation, BPO 4-6 weeks.
No numerical revenue or EBITDA guidance beyond the margin target; management will update on AWS co-sell and EXM/insurance platform progress in Q3.
Alldigi buyback of about INR 48 crore; Digitide's stake is about 73.39%. Proceeds to go predominantly to reduce standalone debt.
capex_capacity: AI lab set up in Bangalore; AI centre of excellence in Coimbatore with 25+ hires.
Two delivery capability centres: Canada (insurance platform) and Chennai (EXM platform).
Philippines BOT mandate: 1,000 hires, about 700 already on board.
Six new live implementations on data, AI and cloud work during Q2.
demand_pricing: TCV ~INR 400 crore in Q2 vs INR 205 crore in Q1; mix shifted toward tech & digital and international.
AI deal share of ACV bookings rose to 29% (INR 160 crore ACV) from 14% (INR 118 crore) in Q1.
Sales funnel rose to INR 170 crore from INR 100 crore in Q1; AI funnel up about 70% QoQ.
Repricing and renegotiation volume up 2.5x QoQ; management is exiting contracts below return thresholds.
India BPM pivoting from T&M/headcount pricing to outcome-based models; AI pitched more in international BPO than India.

qa_highlights.question: Will management give numerical guidance on revenue and EBITDA, and is the 13% exit margin still achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to quality of revenue, sales momentum and mix shift; it reiterated the 200 bps full-year target and said it remains committed, without restating the exit number.

qa_highlights.question: Alldigi buyback size and merger status?
qa_highlights.answer: The Alldigi board proposed a buyback of about INR 48 crore; Digitide holds 73.39% and will receive its share depending on other shareholders' participation. Merger is for the respective boards to decide.

qa_highlights.question: Why are PBT margins squeezed despite high EBITDA, given lease liabilities?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said lease costs hit PBT but not EBITDA; PBT rose to INR 14 crore from INR 12 crore YoY. Issues in India BPM (wage revisions, repricing, walk-aways) will take more than a quarter to fix.

qa_highlights.question: Why not focus on Alldigi's product rather than low-margin tech & digital services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said platforms earn 2-3x BPO profitability and require an ARR/licence go-to-market; EXM business is about INR 150-160 crore, being taken to Middle East, Southeast Asia and SMB.

qa_highlights.question: How is TCV split between new logos and renewals, and how fast does it convert?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not give a new-logo vs renewal split; it said 30-35% of FY27 TCV is expected to convert to revenue this fiscal, with platforms taking 10-16 weeks and BPO 4-6 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: What are the AWS and Anthropic alliance economics?
qa_highlights.answer: AWS partnership is at advanced tier, value currently sub-INR 10 million with a target of 5x at premier tier; first buy-from deal done in US and payroll services sold to AWS in India.

risks_watch: Revenue decline (-2% QoQ) from deliberate exits; sustaining volumes while repricing.
India BPM margin dip to 13.6% and wage/repricing pressure; full-year 200 bps margin target needs H2 delivery.
DSO rose to ~84 days from 82; H2 collections improvement is a key test.
Net cash fell (analyst noted cash drain); no M&A deal yet despite repeated pipeline commentary.
Lease liabilities (H1 ~INR 85 crore) weigh on PBT versus EBITDA.
Q3 updates promised on AWS co-sell, EXM and insurance platform progress.
544413|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on directional progress (TCV, AI revenue, tech & digital margins) but cautious and non-committal on numerical targets, M&A timing and the India BPM turnaround, which management said will take more than a quarter.
key_quotes: Despite the sequential decline, our EBITDA increased to approximately INR 79 crores, up 2.5% Q-on-Q, and the EBITDA margin improved by 45 basis points to 10.4%.
We have continued to re-negotiate contracts and are not shying away to move from businesses that does not meet our return thresholds.
Our TCV booked in the quarter increased by 95% sequentially from INR 205 crores in Q1 to almost INR 400 crores in Q2.
H1 was about putting the foundations in place. H2 is all about converting those foundations into execution, profitable growth, and stronger cash generation.

544414|2026-03.headline: Bluspring FY26 revenue rose 11% to INR 3,304 crore and Q4 EBITDA margin hit 4.2%, with STEAG and LSG acquisitions set to push margins toward 5%.
544414|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue grew 8% YoY to INR 846 crore (flat QoQ) and EBITDA rose 44% YoY to INR 35 crore, with margin up 35 bps QoQ to 4.2%. Adjusted PAT (excluding the Q3 Labour Code one-off) grew 26-27% to INR 67 crore for FY26, and the company reported a net cash position of INR 15 crore at March 2026. Management signed definitive agreements to acquire STEAG Energy Services (India) and LSG Sky Chefs' Bengaluru operations, and guided to 15-16% organic growth in FY27. foundit showed its highest quarterly sales in six quarters (INR 26 crore) and narrowed EBITDA losses to INR 9 crore from INR 12 crore in Q3.

financial_highlights.change: +26-27% YoY, excludes Q3 Labour Code one-off

segments.name: Facility and Food Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 2,031 crore (+12% YoY); Q4 INR 519 crore (+10% YoY, flat QoQ). Q4 EBITDA INR 24 crore (+56% YoY), driven mainly by collections rather than volume; 24 new contracts with INR 124 crore ACV added.

segments.name: Telecom and Industrials
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 615 crore (+7% YoY) with telecom muted by delayed telecom capex; industrial sub-vertical grew 7% QoQ. Q4 revenue INR 157 crore; Q4 EBITDA INR 18 crore (+13% YoY, +19% QoQ); FY26 EBITDA INR 57 crore (+11% YoY).

segments.name: Security Services
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR 659 crore (+14% YoY); Q4 INR 169 crore (+15% YoY, flat QoQ). Headcount crossed 24,000 after about 2,900 guard additions in FY26; FY26 EBITDA INR 19 crore (+23% YoY), Q4 EBITDA INR 6 crore.

segments.name: foundit (investment, shown separately)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 19 crore and sales INR 26 crore (vs average INR 17 crore in Q1-Q3 FY26). EBITDA loss narrowed to INR 9 crore in Q4 from INR 12 crore in Q3; management targets EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 organic revenue growth guided at 15-16%, with organic EBITDA margin around 4%; Q1 is seasonally soft in food and telecom, so margin may dip below 4% before recovering from Q2.
STEAG (about INR 700 crore revenue, high-single-digit EBITDA margin, expected INR 60-65 crore EBITDA) to be consolidated from around end-May 2026; management says closing is expected within the week.
LSG Bengaluru (about INR 110 crore revenue, 17-18% operating margin, about INR 20 crore EBITDA) expected to close in 30-60 days from the call; consolidation for 8-9 months in FY27.

Combined acquisitions expected to add about INR 800 crore annualised revenue and about INR 80 crore EBITDA, taking EBITDA margin toward 5%; management expects PAT above INR 100 crore annualised, excluding foundit.

foundit targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27 (Q4); management says the cost base supports breakeven at INR 34-35 crore revenue run rate, and it will consider monetising part of the stake.
Operating cash flow guided at 55-60% of operating EBITDA. Acquisition debt to be repaid aggressively after integration; funding via debt and internal accruals.
capex_capacity: Management says both acquired businesses are capex-light and does not foresee a large depreciation impact.
STEAG manages about 7 GW of power assets and 2,200 tph of process steam capacity, with over 2,000 employees.
LSG India Bengaluru holds in-flight catering facilities at Bengaluru airport under a concession running to 2039.
Bluspring workforce is above 93,000, up 6,600 during FY26.
demand_pricing: Q4 saw about 42 new contracts with ACV of INR 181 crore; FY26 total was 164 contracts with ACV of INR 459 crore.
Top 30 clients contribute less than 50% of revenue.
Margin gains attributed to new contracts at better margins, better collections and exiting low-margin clients; management says no further low-margin contracts remain to be exited.
Telecom revenue held back by delayed capex from leading telecom operators; industrial metals business gained new contracts at better margins.
Management says bankers and advisers, including big four diligence, drove the Q4 acquisition-related exceptional cost.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA margin reach a sustained 5% after STEAG consolidation, and when will both deals close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said internal estimates put margin in touching distance of 5%. STEAG was expected to close within the week, with consolidation from Q1; LSG was expected in 30-45 days.

qa_highlights.question: Is 15% organic growth realistic given FY26 ACV of about INR 450 crore and contract losses?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said organic growth was about 15-16% in FY26 before lost contracts, some lost to competition and some exited for low margins. It said no further deliberate exits are planned and the sales team is now fully built, supporting 15-16% guidance for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan and funding guardrail for foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Near-term goal is EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27; parent funds the shortfall within visible limits. Management will consider monetising part of the stake, and in the medium term may become a minority investor, once breakeven is reached.

qa_highlights.question: Is STEAG's valuation (INR 180 crore EV, about INR 140 crore cash) sustainable given INR 65 crore EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said STEAG grew from INR 530 crore in FY24 to INR 600 crore in FY25 and INR 700 crore in FY26, with 3-5 year contracts giving about three years of visibility. The seller, a German group, is exiting India to focus on Europe.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pre-Ind AS impact on EBITDA and PAT?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR 10 crore of the INR 121 crore EBITDA is from Ind AS. The only PAT adjustments are the INR 29 crore Labour Code one-off in Q3 and the INR 6.8 crore acquisition cost in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will foundit reach EBITDA neutral and PAT positive, and is the INR 100 crore PAT target ex-foundit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the INR 100 crore PAT target excludes foundit and that breakeven is expected by Q4 FY27. It said PAT-positive operation for foundit would need a run rate of about INR 34-35 crore, with no further people or product investment needed.

risks_watch: Acquisition integration of STEAG and LSG, and delivery of the stated synergies and cross-sell.
Acquisition-related debt repayment pace and funding mix (debt plus internal accruals).
Telecom segment recovery depends on the timing of telecom operators' capex.
foundit: quarter-one seasonality, AI-disruption risk to the talent platform, ongoing parent funding and the monetisation route.
Q1 FY27 margin seasonality in food and telecom may pull margin below 4%.
Management says organic FY27 revenue growth of 15-16% exceeds FY26 ACV-implied growth (about 10-13%), so the target needs to be tested.
544414|2026-03.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on margins, acquisitions and the FY27 organic outlook, and specific on numeric targets. Where questioned on foundit's losses and funding, answers were more hedged, with heavy reliance on timelines and the Q4 sales uptick rather than hard commitments.
key_quotes: And with these acquisitions, our internal estimate is that we should definitely be in the touching distance of 5% margins.
So, internally we've weeded out all those contracts, so we do not believe that the reduction should be of the magnitude that we saw in the year one.
So we are on that trajectory of an internally aligned of taking the company to a EBITDA break-even company by the end of this financial year.

544414|2026-06.headline: Bluspring Q1 FY27 revenue ex-foundit up 20% YoY to INR930 crores; EBITDA INR35 crores (+48% YoY), margin 3.8%, guidance of INR4,700 crores revenue reiterated.
544414|2026-06.overview: Ex-foundit revenue rose 20% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR930 crores, with EBITDA of INR35 crores (+48% YoY, flat QoQ) and PAT of INR16 crores (+47% YoY). STEAG Energy Services was consolidated from May 21, 2026, and contributed INR76 crores to the Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering segment. Management reiterated FY27 guidance (ex-investments) of over INR4,700 crores revenue, over INR200 crores EBITDA and over INR100 crores PAT, and said the LSG Sky Chefs acquisition (INR166 crores) is set to close within weeks. foundit remained loss-making, with a quarterly EBITDA loss of about INR14 crores.

segments.name: Facility and food services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR520 crores (+9% YoY, flat QoQ) and EBITDA INR24 crores (+25% YoY, -3% QoQ); margin 4.6% vs 4.0% a year ago. About 40 new clients added with ACV of about INR89 crores.

segments.name: Security services
segments.commentary: Revenue INR185-187 crores (+24-25% YoY, +10% QoQ) and EBITDA INR5 crores (+37-43% YoY, -12% QoQ); margin 2.8%. Headcount crossed 24,900 after about 900 net adds; 37 new clients with ACV of INR43 crores.

segments.name: Smart Infra, Energy and Engineering (formerly Telecom and Industrial)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR223-229 crores (+47% YoY, +42% QoQ), with STEAG contributing INR76 crores; EBITDA INR21 crores (+80% YoY); margin about 9.2-9.3% vs 8.2%. Telecom was muted on seasonality.

segments.name: foundit
segments.commentary: Revenue INR19 crores with bookings of INR25 crores; EBITDA loss about INR14 crores; cost base about INR32-33 crores. Management guides FY27 cash burn of INR30-35 crores (INR35-40 crores in a later answer) and breakeven by Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 ex-investments: revenue over INR4,700 crores (about 42% YoY), EBITDA over INR200 crores (about 65% YoY), PAT over INR100 crores (about 50% YoY).
Exit FY27 with EBITDA margin above 5%; ROE to rise from about 7% in FY26 to about 13% in FY27. ROE target of 20% and margin of 5.5-6% pulled forward to FY29 from FY30.
STEAG FY27 revenue close to INR1,000 crores at 7-8% EBITDA margin; STEAG's four large contracts add over INR5,100-5,200 crores over five years.
Organic revenue growth guided at 15-16% for FY27.
Net debt/EBITDA below 1x by year-end; acquisition debt about INR150 crores at year-end with organic net debt about zero, though average organic debt of INR150-175 crores.
Effective tax rate guided at about 22%. Working capital days guided to about 45 including STEAG and LSG.
LSG Sky Chefs: about INR110 crores pro forma FY26 revenue, high-teen EBITDA margin, INR125 crores debt to fund; closing in next couple of weeks.
capex_capacity: STEAG acquisition closed May 21, 2026; three of four large contracts live since July 1, the fourth from early August.
LSG India Bengaluru in-flight catering kitchen: concession to operate until 2039; INR112 crores FY26 revenue; debt-free with INR57 crores cash.
Workforce 97,000 at Q1 end, up 3,300 QoQ; crossed about 100,000 in July.
Security headcount above 24,900 after about 900 net adds in the quarter.
demand_pricing: Client vendor consolidation and outsourcing trends cited; management says about two-thirds of facility management is still in-house.
Customer retention about 95%; new business adds about 10% a year; about 4-5% of business lost to competition each year.
STEAG's O&M work is about 90% thermal; management cites about 250 GW of peak demand and STEAG's 14-16 GW portfolio.
Security and FM described as commoditised; STEAG and Hofincons differentiated on German technical pedigree, with plant availability improved from 83-84% to 93-94% for clients.
Telecom softness in Q1, with early July rollout signs from large players; management expects better H2 telecom.
Food margins range 5-10% by segment; aviation catering at the high end. LPG price increases pressured food margins.

qa_highlights.question: How will management run the three divisions over the next two years, and what is the addressable market for STEAG-type contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Each of the three businesses has its own leadership team and board-set growth targets. Management cites vendor consolidation, outsourcing (about two-thirds of FM still in-house) and GST/Labour Code formalisation. STEAG's large contracts are end-to-end outcome-based O&M, combining STEAG, Hofincons and the FM team.

qa_highlights.question: What is the foundit path to breakeven and how much more funding is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets Q4 FY27 breakeven. Cost base is about INR32-33 crores and will not rise. FY27 cash burn guided at INR35-40 crores in one answer, versus INR30-35 crores in the prepared remarks. Breakeven needs quarterly sales above INR35-40 crores, with revenue recognised from subscriptions over a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did foundit sales of about INR10 crores more over two quarters not show up in revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said B2B subscription revenue is deferred and recognised as service is consumed, with sales-to-revenue ratio of about 15-18%. Leakage fell from about 40% to about 20%. Revenue rose from INR17-18 crores to INR19 crores, with INR21 crores expected next and INR22-23 crores in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise to INR108 crores from INR78 crores QoQ, and what is the run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The jump is mainly subcontracting in telecom and STEAG. The CFO said the new base should hold for the next 2-3 quarters given STEAG.

qa_highlights.question: What are the STEAG contract economics: FY27 revenue, margin and five-year sustainability after the initial term?
qa_highlights.answer: STEAG FY27 revenue is close to INR1,000 crores at 7-8% EBITDA margin, with consolidation from May 21. Contracts run five years with extension options. Plant availability improved from 83-84% to 93-94% for clients, which management cites as the basis for renewal.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and are there deposits for large deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Organic working capital days are about 37. Including STEAG and the large contracts, management guided about 45 days, with a possible rise of about eight days before it settles. Power contracts need non-funded bank guarantees, not cash deposits.

qa_highlights.question: How do long-term margin and ROE targets change after the acquisitions, and what is the ELI scheme impact?
qa_highlights.answer: The 20% ROE and 5.5-6% EBITDA margin targets are kept but pulled forward from FY30 to mostly FY29. Management has seen no substantial ELI scheme benefit so far.

risks_watch: foundit: sustained losses, a cash burn guide that moved from INR30-35 crores to INR35-40 crores, and breakeven by Q4 FY27 that depends on sales converting to revenue.

Telecom softness in Q1; recovery depends on capex revival from Q2 and H2 FY27 telecom orders.
Debt: net debt INR172 crores, acquisition debt about INR150 crores at year end, and LSG INR125 crores debt funding due within weeks.
Execution and renewal of STEAG's four large five-year contracts, and the fourth contract starting from early August.

We feel that we have a phenomenal opportunity.

So, we are hopeful that the second half of the year including quarter 2 for telecom should be better, and which means telecom as a whole for our portfolio should do better year-on-year from an overall revenue and EBITDA standpoint.
We expect the EBITDA burn for the financial year to be in the range of INR30 crores to INR35 crores.

PAT was INR 20 crore versus INR 5 crore a year earlier. Management attributed margin expansion to a mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, whose combined share rose from about 46% to 63%. Net working capital days fell to 56 from 66 at March 2026 (about 97 in the prior quarter per an analyst exchange), and management reiterated 35-40% annual growth guidance.

segments.commentary: Contributed about INR 28 crore, roughly 10% of top line, in Q1. New INR 650 crore mandate from Wadhwa Group (Mumbai); GDV under execution rose to over INR 1,800 crore from INR 1,250 crore at Q4 FY26. Management cited 60-65% EBITDA margin for DaaS.

qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain is mainly mix: contract manufacturing and DaaS, which carry higher margins than B2B, rose from about 46% to 63% of revenue; management expects this to sustain for the next few quarters. Directionally, 11% next year was agreed as fair.

qa_highlights.question: How much utilisation headroom is left in contract manufacturing and how will capacity grow?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is 65-70% on about 9 million tonnes; 2-3 million tonnes to be added in the next two quarters by recycling existing deposits, taking capacity to about 11 million tonnes.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 35-40% guidance be raised, given Q1 and Q2 are seasonally lean?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is sticking to 35-40% annual growth; first six months about 40% of sales and second half about 60%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the credit losses and loss given default?
qa_highlights.answer: Cumulative ECL about INR 22 crore on about INR 3,800-4,000 crore lifetime revenue. Recoveries after legal process range from 25% to over 80%, and most new receivables are insured.

qa_highlights.question: How does supply chain financing work and does it cost interest?
qa_highlights.answer: Financiers pay vendors on day one and the company gets about 90 days to pay; interest is sometimes borne by vendors and is negotiated. Management said it accepts the interest cost to reduce working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Does DaaS expose the company to real estate risk and how is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not a RERA promoter and does not lend or commit capital; income is a fixed monthly fee, a percentage of construction and a percentage of sales, with financial closure and bank loans in place on day one.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt path and what drives the rise to INR 75-80 crore?

qa_highlights.question: How concentrated is the customer base and what is the DaaS sales commission benchmark?
qa_highlights.answer: Top 10 customers are 45-50% of revenue, spread across projects and regions. Management cited sales-only channels charging 2-3% and some 4-5% of GDV, arguing DaaS covers far more than sales.

544420|2026-06.headline: Raymond Realty Q1 FY27 booking value rose 129% YoY to INR700 crore; FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth and 17-19% EBITDA margin reiterated.
544420|2026-06.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 booking value of INR700 crore (up 129% YoY), customer collections of INR550 crore (up 47%) and total income of INR536 crore (up 37%). EBITDA rose 70% YoY to INR70 crore, with margin expanding from 11% to 13%, which management attributed to upfront costs from four projects launched in Q4 FY26. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20%+ presales growth, 20%+ revenue growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin and 20%+ ROCE. JDAs now account for about 52% of INR52,000 crore total GDV, and a new Parel JDA with INR8,500 crore GDV was signed.

management said FY27 interest INR100-120 crore

segments.name: Owned land (Thane, 100 acres)
segments.commentary: 65 acres under active development with 6.7 million sq ft RERA carpet area and INR16,500 crore revenue potential; INR9,400 crore sold and INR7,460 crore collected to date. Contributed 36% of Q1 booking value; 11 towers (about 4,000 homes) delivered. Management expects own-land margins of 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: What are the top execution priorities and biggest risks (demand, regulation, competition)?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is execution of Q4 FY26 launches; demand 'pleasantly' above expectations; cost pressures from global wars seen as temporary, with contingencies budgeted over 5-6 year project cycles; policy stable with DCR 2034 and supportive Maharashtra government.

qa_highlights.question: How is capital allocation and funding aligned with the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt-to-equity 0.7x versus internal 1x ceiling; AIFs offering SPV-level capital as an option; equity seen as last resort; cost of debt has only declined.

qa_highlights.question: Parel project ticket size, saleable area, launch timing and realisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Launch about 18 months away; ticket sizes INR6-20 crore; total GDV INR8,500 crore; realisation not disclosed beyond GDV.

qa_highlights.question: Mahim launch timing and GDV, and H2 launch calendar?
qa_highlights.answer: Two Mahim projects: first ~Nov-Dec 2026 (~INR2,500 crore GDV), second Feb-Mar 2027 (~INR2,100-2,200 crore); six of eight JDAs to be launched by FY27 end.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose of TenX Mahalakshmi Limited incorporation?
qa_highlights.answer: Incorporated as an SPV in anticipation of new projects; no deal signed yet, to be disclosed when signed.

qa_highlights.question: JDA vs owned-land economics, margins and ROCE?
qa_highlights.answer: JDA capital need INR300-350 crore per project, peak INR450-500 crore for Parel; own land margin 25-26%, JDA ~20% scaling up in FY28; ROCE guided at 20%+.

qa_highlights.question: Interest cost trajectory and debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt INR824 crore, gross debt INR1,095 crore, cash INR271 crore; FY27 interest INR100-120 crore; Q1 ~INR47 crore; government dues interest at 8-9% explained as part of finance cost.

qa_highlights.question: Why no PAT guidance and what about cash profit and operating cash flow?
qa_highlights.answer: No net profit or operating cash flow guidance given; management will revert on PAT growth impact of higher interest.

qa_highlights.question: Demand softness and Home Fest purpose?
qa_highlights.answer: No softness seen; Home Fest is an annual monsoon event for top-of-funnel; response described as good.

qa_highlights.question: Expansion beyond MMR and JDA control terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus remains MMR and Maharashtra; Pune studied but returns did not meet criteria. Company insists on 100% development control in JDAs with step-in rights.

544420|2026-09.headline: Raymond Realty Q2 FY27 total income rose 7% YoY to INR757 crore, EBITDA margin 15%, booking value up 111% YoY in H1 to INR1,602 crore.
544420|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income grew 7% YoY to INR757 crore and EBITDA rose to INR115 crore at a 15% margin versus 14% a year earlier. Quarterly pre-sales nearly doubled with no new launches, and H1 booking value reached INR1,602 crore (+111% YoY) while collections rose 67% to INR682 crore in Q2. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 20% pre-sales growth, 17-19% EBITDA margin, 20% ROCE and 9-10% PAT margin, and dropped explicit revenue growth guidance. An ICICI Prudential AIF subsidiary investment of INR210 crore for the Mahim project and a INR400 crore promoter equity infusion were announced, with debt held near INR1,200 crore.

544421|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA of ~260m (30% margin) included ~46m of one-offs; adjusted ~304m (35%), with gases segment margin 40% in Q4 and 38.4% for FY26.
544421|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 reported EBITDA was about 260 million at a roughly 30% margin, but management cited three non-recurring items totalling about 46 million (leave-encashment provision 11m, impairment on a legacy non-core investment, and a 15m settlement with an on-site customer over plant start-up date), taking adjusted EBITDA to about 304 million (about 35%). Core gases segment revenue grew 9% QoQ in Q4, and FY26 core gases revenue grew 14.2% over FY25, with reported growth held back by the delayed start of Uluberia 2. Argon prices recovered from Q3 lows but remain below 1H FY26 levels. Management framed FY27 as an execution year with a stronger capacity base, but gave no numeric guidance beyond a 20% revenue CAGR target over the next 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.answer: Q4 prices recovered from Q3 but are below 1H FY26; management urged viewing argon on an annual average basis and expects it to remain robust with steel-sector demand.

qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated a 20% revenue CAGR over the next 2-3 years, with no single-year guidance, supported by the Uluberia 2 and East India on-site plants and further merchant additions.

544421|2026-06.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to ₹987 mn and EBITDA margin reached 39%, with PAT up 87% YoY to ₹350 mn.
544421|2026-06.overview: Ellenbarrie posted a strong Q1 FY27, with revenue from operations of ₹987 mn (+18% YoY, +13% QoQ), driven mainly by ramp-up of the Kurnool and Uluberia 2 plants. EBITDA rose to ₹387 mn (+21% YoY, +50% QoQ) at a 39% margin, which management attributed mainly to new power-efficient capacity, cost control and higher production rather than argon pricing. PAT of ₹350 mn was helped by lower finance cost and a lower effective tax rate. Management reaffirmed FY27 capex of ₹250 crore and FY28 capex of ₹200 crore, and said the East India 320 TPD on-site plant should start contributing revenue in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said merchant plants are not pre-contracted; the site is chosen after a micro-market survey, contracting starts 3–4 months before commissioning, and the ramp to 80–90% utilisation takes 18–24 months. Early focus is on customers located near their factories, where the company has a cost advantage, plus new industries in the area.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the ₹450 crore is for two merchant plants: North India (not yet operational) and West Central India (construction started). Together they are about 450–500 TPD. The entire residual amount of the ₹450 crore goes to these two plants.

qa_highlights.answer: Power is the largest cost. Management cited newer, more efficient plants that use less power per unit of gas, plus one long-term renewable PPA signed, exchange purchases, and ongoing scouting for more long-term PPAs. Other costs such as employee and other expenses were described as having standard annual increases.

544421|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to ₹1,143 mn, but consolidated EBITDA margin fell to ~36% from 39% on freight and employee costs.
544421|2026-09.overview: Revenue from operations was ₹1,143 mn, up 28% YoY and 16% QoQ, with H1 FY27 revenue at ₹2,130 mn (+23%). Consolidated EBITDA rose to ₹407 mn from ₹387 mn in Q1, but margin slipped to ~36% from ~39%, which management attributed to diesel-linked transport costs, longer-distance deliveries and employee costs (including increment arrears and project engineering build-out). Core gases segment margin improved to ~39% from 38%. The 325 TPD Durgapur on-site plant was commissioned in September 2026, and a ₹480 crore BHEL EPC contract for a 1,200 TPD air separation unit in Odisha was won, with commissioning expected in FY29.

544423|2026-03.headline: Kalpataru Q4 FY26 revenue rose to INR 1,694 crore (~3x YoY) on handovers; FY26 pre-sales INR 5,280 crore, up 17%, with no formal FY27 guidance yet.

Q4 pre-sales hit a record INR 1,833 crore (+6% YoY) and collections a record INR 1,487 crore (+41%). FY26 collections grew 34% to INR 4,960 crore, and net debt was INR 8,106 crore (net debt-to-equity about 2x). management also cited 36% margin for full year; figures as stated on call

financial_highlights.value: INR 1,002 crore (100% basis about INR 1,500 crore)

segments.name: MMR (Mumbai Metro Region)

segments.commentary: Together expected to contribute about INR 3,500 crore of inflows from ongoing projects. Kalpataru Blossoms (Pune) may launch in two phases. Hyderabad has one project, described as performing well.

FY27 delivery target of about 5.5 million sq ft; visibility on cash flows for the next 12 months.
FY27 new launches of about 5 million sq ft, GDV about INR 7,800 crore; launch-phase sales target 20-25%; expected FY27 launch sales INR 1,800-2,000 crore.
Net debt to stay at or below the March 2026 level of INR 8,100 crore in FY27, with a marginal absolute reduction targeted; debt-to-equity to be below 2x.

Further refinancing of about INR 1,300 crore expected in the coming quarter, following about INR 3,500 crore refinanced since listing (120 bps lower blended cost of debt, about INR 125 crore annual savings).

FY26 launches: four tower phases in three projects (Eternia, Aria, Shristi Namaah) plus Estella, totalling 1.8 million sq ft. Some launches slipped to H1 FY27 pending approvals.
New BD: redevelopment of Shri Mahalakshmi CHS, Andheri West, about 3 acres, about 0.4 million sq ft carpet area, GDV about INR 1,400 crore.
Construction cost FY26: INR 1,916 crore at 100% level; Kalpataru share INR 1,512 crore. Projects are fully financially closed.

demand_pricing: Q4 footfalls and walk-ins described as good, with April also robust; barring an April vacation period and a geopolitical slowdown, no drastic change seen.

Construction cost inflation of 2-4% attributed to the Middle East crisis, with tile and pipe supply issues resolved; management expects no material impact on sales value.

qa_highlights.answer: Not more than 20% of the INR 1,062 crore closing cash balance is locked in RERA accounts; the rest is free for projects.

qa_highlights.answer: Revenue-level margins of 20-25%, with cash margins of 25-30% because land acquisition payments are largely done. Management said nothing further is needed for the pipeline, with project-level capex data to follow offline.

rows.why: Unsold inventory in ongoing projects is about INR 22,000 crore and could rise to about INR 30,000 crore with another INR 7,000-8,000 crore added in FY27, which ties up cash even as collections grow.

544423|2026-09.headline: Kalpataru Q2 FY27 pre-sales fell 5% to INR 1,258 crore, but FY27 pre-sales guidance of INR 6,500 crore was held unchanged.

segments.name: Sports infrastructure

Stadium revenue to date was about INR30-35 crore, and completion is targeted in about 15 months.

Management described competition as healthy with decent margins, not heavy under-bidding.

544425|2026-06.headline: AJC Jewel Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 124.69% YoY to Rs 101.38 crore; EBITDA margin 4.58% and PAT margin 2.35%.
544425|2026-06.overview: Consolidated revenue reached Rs 101.38 crore versus Rs 45.12 crore in Q1 FY26, with EBITDA of Rs 4.64 crore (from Rs 1.58 crore) and PAT of Rs 2.38 crore (from Rs 0.57 crore). Margins expanded, with EBITDA margin at 4.58% (from 3.5%) and PAT margin at 2.35% (from 1.26%). Management announced a proposed 80% stake acquisition in AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC, Sharjah, via a non-cash share swap valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore, though the Sharjah entity is not consolidated in Q1. Management guided FY27 standalone India revenue of Rs 450 crore and 50% CAGR for three years, on a volume basis. Many answers on utilisation, Esthara economics and FY28 targets were deferred to H1 results.

segments.name: India gold jewellery (core B2B, casting)
segments.commentary: Capacity 5 kg/day; utilisation about 25% (about 1.2 kg/day). Kerala accounts for 90-95% of revenue. Top 10 customers are about 50% of revenue; about 200 other customers make up the rest.

segments.name: Sharjah UAE (AJC Jewel Manufacturers FZC)
segments.commentary: Gold jewellery capacity 3 kg/day at about 800 g/day (about 27% utilisation). Management cited PAT margin of about 4% and EBITDA margin of about 5%, in a tax-exempt free zone. Not consolidated in Q1; expected consolidation from Q3.

segments.name: Esthara Jewels (silver DTC)
segments.commentary: Three stores operational in Kerala; two more under fit-out, expected to open by end of next month. Silver capacity 8 kg/day with about 1 kg/day production. Management targets about Rs 20 lakh revenue per store per month; first store reportedly about Rs 15 lakh per month. Capex about Rs 4,000 per sq ft; opex about Rs 5-6 lakh per store; breakeven targeted within one year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone India revenue target of Rs 450 crore (management reiterated it is standalone India only; Sharjah additional).
Revenue growth of about 50% CAGR for the next three years, stated as based on volume growth; management said price effects would be added only if gold prices rise.
Current PAT margin of about 2.5% cited for the year.
Sharjah full-year contribution to be updated after H1 results; acquisition completion expected in 3-6 months subject to BSE and regulatory approvals.
Dilution to existing shareholders from the share swap estimated at about 7-8%, per management (uncertain).
Store count and three-year store plans to be updated post H1 results.
Q1 and Q2 seasonally moderate; Q3 and Q4 stronger on festivals and weddings.
capex_capacity: India: 5 kg/day gold casting capacity, upgraded from IPO proceeds to 120% expansion (cited as 5 kg Kerala, 8 kg silver), with about 25% utilisation today.
Silver jewellery production started in India; capacity up to 8 kg/day, currently about 1 kg/day.
Sharjah: 3 kg/day installed gold capacity at about 800 g/day.
At 100% utilisation management cited India about Rs 7 crore/day (about Rs 2,500 crore/yr at 5 kg/day) and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day; these are indicative and not guidance.
Additional working capital needed to reach peak utilisation; to be funded via internal accruals, debt and possibly equity, gradually.
Design and innovation centre set up; about 20 in-house design staff; library of about 2.5 lakh designs on B2B portal.
demand_pricing: Added 12 independent jewellers in Q1, mainly mid and small Kerala retailers; no new corporate clients after Kalyan.
Management is targeting expansion beyond Kerala, with a marketing team in Chennai; international orders to be served via Sharjah.
Management said gold price moves will not affect margins because it hedges with suppliers and on MCX.
Launched 9-karat and 18-karat products; 18-karat is served to some customers for higher margin at lower caratage. Early response described as encouraging.
Management said no gold metal loan or advance gold loan business; no bullion trading in consolidated revenue.
Receivables growth well ahead of sales (3-year receivables CAGR about 51% vs sales 16%), attributed to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods.

qa_highlights.answer: 80% stake via share swap, valued at up to Rs 9.6 crore; Sharjah earns about 4% PAT and about 5% EBITDA, aided by free-zone tax exemption. Completion expected in 3-6 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the 50% growth guidance based on, volume or price?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume only; price changes would be added only if gold prices rise.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected utilisation for FY27/FY28 and revenue at 100% utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: No utilisation guidance given. Indicative values at 100%: India about Rs 7 crore/day and Sharjah about Rs 3.6 crore/day. FY27 India target is Rs 450 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why is receivables growth far ahead of sales?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to recent corporate clients with longer credit periods, and said it will try to reduce debtors.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will try to make it positive in coming years, without a specific timeline; focus is on sales volume and growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a demand impact from the duty change talk and what is the Q2/Q3 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said duty changes have not affected the business historically; Q1 and Q2 are moderate, Q3 and Q4 stronger. No specific Q3 numbers given.

544429|2026-03.headline: HDB Financial Q4 FY26: PAT rose 16.6% QoQ to ₹751 crore, NIM expanded to 8.23% and Gross Stage 3 fell to 2.44%.
544429|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 showed sequential improvement on profitability, margins and asset quality. Disbursements hit a record ₹19,922 crore (up 11.2% QoQ), but gross loan book growth was only 3.4% QoQ and 10.9% YoY. NIM rose 16 bps QoQ to 8.23%, helped by lower borrowing costs, while yield dipped 7-8 bps on product mix. Management said March went well and it has not yet seen level 2/3 impact from the West Asia conflict, which it flagged as a key monitorable.

vs 41.6% in Q3 FY26, 42.9% in Q4 FY25
vs 2.81% at Dec 31, 2025 and at Mar 31, 2025 per Q&A

segments.name: Enterprise lending
segments.commentary: Q4 disbursements grew ~27.9% QoQ and ~15.4% YoY. LAP+EBL book grew 3.8% QoQ on ~36% disbursement growth. Enterprise lending Stage 3 fell to 1.58% from 1.82% in Q3 and 1.79% a year ago.

segments.name: Asset finance (CV/CE)
segments.commentary: Book showed moderate growth in Q4. Gross Stage 3 moved 3.14% (Q4 FY25) to 4.3% (Q3 FY26) to 3.79% (Q4 FY26). FY26 disbursements declined ~3% per analyst; management is pushing used vehicles, with a 50:50 new/used target over four years.

segments.name: Consumer finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 5.3% QoQ and 19.4% YoY, led by consumer durables then auto loans. Stage 3 rose to 2.44% from 2.26% a year ago, but improved from Q3.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: Gold loan book doubled in FY26; disbursements grew 58.7% QoQ.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term growth target: nominal GDP + 6-7% CAGR, with the three-year agenda; management declined to give specific numbers.
Credit cost to moderate to around 2.3% (+/- ) and be sustainable at that level over the medium term.
NIM to be maintained at 8% or above, described as non-negotiable in 2/3/5-year plans; Q4 was 8.23%.
FY27 opex-to-gross loan book expected around 3.7% (FY26 was ~3.8%); cost-to-income guided to a similar range.
Cost of borrowings expected to hold for at least the current quarter; the CP mix is low and bank loans are below 50% of borrowings.
Expects Q1 to be seasonally slower; comparisons should be made Q1 vs Q1, not Q1 vs Q4. Ambition is YoY disbursement growth of 18-20%, described as hopeful, not committed.
capex_capacity: Branch count at 1,730 across 1,161 towns and cities; 20-30 branches may be added or relocated, with consolidation into larger formats (600-800 sq ft to up to 4,000 sq ft).
Management said no square footage has been reduced in the last three quarters as a listed company.
DIY digital sourcing grew ~2.2x in FY26; management expects it to grow further (2x to 5x cited).
App downloads at 1.41 crore; 4.76 lakh daily active users.
Five large AI-powered initiatives underway; bot-based collections nudging covered over 50% of early-bucket customers needing a nudge in Q4, improving early-bucket collection efficiency by ~25 bps.
demand_pricing: Management says all product yields were held in Q4; the 7-8 bps yield decline was from product mix, with unsecured disbursement growth lagging. Yield should return with unsecured growth, staying within the 14%+ range.
Q2, Q3 and Q4 FY26 disbursements were ₹15,599 crore, ₹17,917 crore and ₹19,922 crore respectively.
Secured share of gross loans is 74%, up from the 72% level management has held historically.
Borrowing costs have risen across the market over the past month, per management; the company has no low-cost borrowings left to reset after the last tranche in Oct-Nov 2025.
Average exposure per customer is ~₹1.66 lakh; the retail book is 100% of the portfolio.
AUM mix is 38:38:24 (enterprise lending : asset finance : consumer finance), expected to move to roughly 38:37:25 in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: What changed in March and early April on the West Asia conflict, supply chains and CV operators?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said March went well and is reflected in the results; no level 2/3 impact seen so far. It remains a key monitorable, with a 15-20 day watch period.

qa_highlights.question: Were contingency or buffer provisions considered for MSME/SME stress?
qa_highlights.answer: No specific level 2/3 impact seen yet. Management said LAP and MSME challenges were resolved by the March quarter and the focus is now growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 35 bps QoQ fall in cost of funds and can it be sustained given market rates?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it held lending rates and worked on borrowing strategies; no low-cost borrowings remain to reset. Cost of funds should hold for the current quarter, though market rates have risen.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Stage 1 PCR rise by 30 bps, and why did enterprise lending PCR fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Provisioning is refreshed quarterly on an automated ECL basis (fully automated this quarter) using PD, LGD and product mix. Management said there is no one-time item.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset finance Stage 3 recover so quickly?
qa_highlights.answer: Recovery has been K-shaped: accounts challenged in Q1 recovered slowly, while newer slippages are recovering faster. Management pushed recoveries and flow-forward reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM be sustained at 8%+ and what about branch additions?
qa_highlights.answer: 8%+ NIM is non-negotiable in internal plans; Q4 was 8.23%. Branch count will change by 20-30 sites through consolidation and upsizing, with digital channels driving growth.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict, supply chain disruption and El Nino impact on CV and MSME repayments; management says it is too early to call second- and third-order effects.

Asset finance Stage 3 at 3.79% and consumer finance Stage 3 at 2.44%; sustainability of the recovery and the used-vehicle push.

Yield dilution from product mix until unsecured business loans regain growth.

544429|2026-06.headline: HDB Financial Q1 FY27 PAT rose 38.3% YoY to ₹785 crores, a record, with Stage 3 down to 2.34% and NIM at 8.35%.
544429|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 delivered record quarterly profit of ₹785 crores (up 38.3% YoY, 4.6% QoQ) with ROA of 2.5% and ROE of 15%. Gross Stage 3 improved to 2.34% from 2.44% in March 2026 and 2.56% a year earlier, and credit cost held at 2.32% versus 2.35% in Q4. Loan book grew 11.3% YoY to ₹1,21,846 crores but only 2.8% QoQ, with Asset Finance and Business Loans still lagging. Management pushed growth recovery into Q2–Q3 and kept the 2.3% steady-state credit cost and 8%+ NIM framing without formal annual guidance.

Gold loan book doubled YoY, with about 500 branches enabled; Unsecured Business Loans disbursements began accelerating late in the quarter, while the book shrank marginally QoQ.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book grew 10% YoY and construction equipment 8% YoY; disbursements remain the laggard. Management reduced high-value, low-return products (tractor trailers, high-end HCVs), and says Stage 3 improved sequentially.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Book grew 7.5% QoQ and 21% YoY; consumer durables grew over 50% YoY on compressor season demand, and auto loans grew 21% YoY. Auto is flagged as the area needing more growth.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give formal guidance; steady-state credit cost viewed at about 2.3%, with a possible decline only if the economy improves.
NIM expected to hold at 8%+ and focus remains 2.5% ROA on a consistent basis.
Business Loans book expected to turn positive QoQ from Q2 and show YoY growth from Q3; Q2 expected to be positive in direction.
Cost of funds expected to be range-bound in Q2; Q3 view deferred. Current ratio about 1.3x and CP book under 2%.
Asset Finance growth expected to pick up over the next three to four quarters, with July run rate improving if the trend holds.
Viral Shah's 18% growth question was not answered; management said it would revert closer to dates.
capex_capacity: Gold loans: about 500+ branches enabled; management says the existing network could roughly double gold loans over time, with the timing still under internal work.
Distribution footprint of about 1.6 lakh+ retail touchpoints across about 1,200 cities; relationships with 150+ consumer durable manufacturers.
Rural micro-finance run through a couple of hundred branches as a small pilot; management declined to say whether it would be shut down.
Customer franchise 23.9 million, up 18.6% YoY and 4.1% QoQ.
demand_pricing: Q1 disbursements ₹17,629 crores, up 16.2% YoY; gross loan book ₹1,21,846 crores, up 11.3% YoY and 2.8% QoQ; secured loans 73.9% of book.
May 2026 was the highest-ever volume for a large number of Asset Finance products management wants to grow.
Yields described as fairly constant; Q1 yield uptick attributed to product mix (consumer durables seasonality), not to pricing.
Competition: management declined to name who is taking up the Asset Finance segments it is vacating.
Fuel price increases of about 8–9% reportedly passed on in small doses; freight rates described as stable for its customer base.
ECLGS uptake described as work in progress and modest; eligibility requires working capital end-use.
Top 20 customers are about 0.3% of AUM, so the book is retail-weighted.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance disbursement lagging and when will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Used CV build-out and product reprioritisation are largely done, and growth should show over the next few quarters; July run rate improvement was expected but not quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the full-year credit cost guidance for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not guide; 2.3% is the steady-state view, with a possible decline only if economic conditions improve. Current metrics are comfortable, and check bounce for June–July was described as fine.

qa_highlights.question: Why are Business Loans, MFI and two-wheeler books shrinking QoQ?

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Asset Finance Stage 3 level and can it fall toward 3%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline is on a flat book; Stage 3 should fall as the book grows and as the economy improves, and it was steady so far in June-July.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a cost-of-funds outlook and liquidity strategy?

qa_highlights.question: Is the yield uptick in Q1 seasonal?
qa_highlights.answer: The uptick is purely product mix, driven by the consumer durables compressor season; yields are otherwise stable, and the next peak is Dussehra-Diwali.

544429|2026-09.headline: HDB Financial Q2 FY27 PAT rose 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, NIM 8.23%, Stage 3 down to 2.43%, with management guiding to a near-term 8.2%+ NIM.
544429|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 showed disbursements up 18.7% YoY to ₹18,522 crore and PAT up 34% YoY to ₹780 crore, with Stage 3 improving YoY to 2.43%. Gross loan book grew 11.7% YoY to ₹1,24,469 crore, which management described as slow relative to disbursements because of high repayments. Sequentially, NIM was 8.23% versus 8.35% in Q1, and credit cost rose to 2.37%, with Stage 2 build-up in Asset Finance (mainly used/new CV) flagged as seasonal. The 25 bps repo hike on October 7, 2026 is the main near-term margin variable; management expects a minor impact in Q3 and aims to hold NIM at 8.2%+ in the near term.

financial_highlights.change: vs 7.95% in Q2FY26 and 8.35% in Q1FY27
vs 40.7% in Q2FY26 and 39.9% in Q1FY27

segments.name: Enterprise Lending
segments.commentary: Disbursements grew 25.5% YoY; LAP+EBL (mortgage) disbursements up 30% YoY, LAP growing about 3-3.5% QoQ. Gold loan disbursements up over 60% YoY, unsecured business loans turned slightly positive QoQ (+0.2%) after six quarters.

segments.name: Asset Finance
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicle book up 8% YoY and construction equipment up 12% YoY. New CV is hitting budget, while used CV growth is weak and is being addressed through internal actions; CV and CE drove the Stage 2 build-up.

segments.name: Consumer Finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements up over 25% YoY and book up 22% YoY. Consumer durables book up 49% YoY, auto loans up 22%, relationship personal loans up 16%.

guidance_outlook: Management expects NIM to hold in a narrow range, targeting at least 8.2%+ in the near term and 8%+ over the long term; minor impact expected in Q3 from the 25 bps repo hike.
Disbursement trajectory expected to rise, with Q3 better than Q2 and Q4 better than Q3; management hopes Q4 shows growth in the 17-18% range, though it did not commit to a number.
Medium-term credit cost target of 2.3% +/- range; Q2 credit cost of 2.37% described as a 5 bps uptick expected to reverse.
ROA target of 2.5%+ on an annualised basis in the short to medium term.

AI-led customer onboarding started in consumer finance; over 1 in 5 early-bucket collection calls now handled by an AI bot.
Average ticket size about ₹4.6 million for LAP and ₹1.4 million for enterprise business loans; EBL offered in more than 800 cities.

qa_highlights.question: Why did asset yields moderate QoQ despite strong consumer finance growth, and how will cost of funds and NIM trend if repo rises 75-100 bps?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 is seasonally about 10-12 bps higher on NIM. Management said NIM came in 1-2 bps above plan, excluding an extra day in Q2, and expects only a minor Q3 impact, with LAP floating-rate pass-through and Q3 product mix as offsets.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Asset Finance growth weak, is the problem in new or used CV?
qa_highlights.answer: New CV is hitting budget; used CV is the issue, with a combination of internal challenges and weak market demand. Delinquencies in the older book have not yet come off.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the Stage 2 build-up in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to CV, and slightly to CE, as seasonal and expected to revert in the coming quarter. Management said the rise was 9 bps QoQ and that faster book growth would have shown about 2 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Will drought and macro conditions in key states affect Asset Finance and the credit cost guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is monitoring impacts, with a small tractor exposure in drought-declared areas. Credit cost is managed within 2.3% +/-, and it could fall about 5 bps next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for Asset Finance growth and FY28 growth, and the risk to NIM plus fee income from the insurance commission proposal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes growth will return to the industry median, citing capacity and network readiness; FY26 disbursement growth was 3%. On fees, the company is still assessing the proposal, with ₹455 crore of insurance-related income at stake.

544430|2026-03.headline: Sambhv Steel Tubes Q4 FY26 revenue rose 38% to INR685 crores and EBITDA 91% to INR92 crores, with record quarterly profit.
544430|2026-03.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue, EBITDA and PAT for Q4 FY26, with EBITDA per ton at INR9,500 excluding sponge iron sales, helped by raw-material lag and firm HR coil prices. For FY26, sales volume rose 37% to 3,96,000 tons, revenue 60% to INR2,413 crores and PAT more than doubled to INR143 crores. Capex was raised: the Kesda stainless steel Phase 1 (3,60,000 tpa) is on track for Q4 FY27, plus an additional INR200 crores of brownfield and power/DFT projects. Management guided Q1 FY27 EBITDA per ton to INR7,500-8,000 and FY27 average to INR7,000-8,000.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 EBITDA per ton so high, and what is sustainable?

qa_highlights.question: Is the stainless steel production versus sales gap explained?

544430|2026-06.headline: Sambhv Q1 FY27 revenue INR732 crore (+31% YoY), EBITDA INR100 crore, PAT INR56 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided INR7,500-8,500.

The Kuthrel stainless CR coil debottlenecking doubled capacity to 116,000 tpa, and the Kesda greenfield project is guided for Q4 FY27 commissioning. FY27 revenue and EBITDA growth of 10-15% over FY26; FY26 operating EBITDA base cited as about INR270 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What will peak debt, finance cost and cost of debt look like after Kesda?

qa_highlights.question: Is the Kesda Q4 FY27 timeline achievable through monsoon?

qa_highlights.question: Rationale for the INR100 crore warrant issue?

qa_highlights.question: Why co-branding for stainless pipes instead of direct sales?

qa_highlights.question: Stainless CR coil margin and HR coil margin?

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 EBITDA growth guided at only 10-15% given the stainless ramp?

qa_highlights.question: Working capital needs and capex schedule?

544430|2026-09.headline: Sambhv Q2 FY27 revenue INR840 crore, EBITDA INR105 crore (>12% margin), PAT INR61 crore; FY27 EBITDA/ton guided at INR8,000-8,500.
544430|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR840 crore, EBITDA of INR105 crore, PAT of INR61 crore and operating cash flow of INR213 crore, with value-added sales volume up 27% YoY. EBITDA per ton fell from about INR8,800 in Q1 to about INR8,200 in Q2, attributed to monsoon-related raw material yield losses, stainless steel margin compression from Chinese 200/300 series dumping after QCO relaxation, and normalising Q1 prices. Management raised its FY27 EBITDA/ton bracket to INR8,000-8,500 and announced a seamless stainless steel pipe project (INR150 crore, 14,400 tpa, production by March 2028). Working capital days fell to 4-5, which management said is not sustainable versus a 20-25 day norm.

segments.name: MS pipes and tubes
segments.commentary: Largest contributor to volume growth in Q2; EBITDA per ton cited at about INR9,000. Q2 realisation about INR60-61/kg-equivalent per management, guided to INR63-64 for Q3.

segments.name: Galvanised / coated products
segments.commentary: EBITDA per ton cited at about INR7,000. Q3 realisation guided at INR78-79 for GP coil and pipe, versus INR72-73 in Q2.

segments.name: Stainless steel (flat/coil)
segments.commentary: Production about 5,000-5,500 tons per month; EBITDA about INR12,000-13,000 per ton, down from Q1 due to Chinese dumping. Mix about 90% 200 series and 10% 300 series. Q2 volumes cited as 130,000 tons (200 series) and 230,000 tons (300 series).

segments.name: Seamless stainless steel pipes (new)
segments.commentary: Planned 14,400 tpa piercing and pilgering plant, INR150 crore capex, production expected by March 2028. Management targets about 10,000 tons by FY30 and an EBITDA of INR60-70 crore at steady state.

FY27 EBITDA per ton bracket raised to INR8,000-8,500.
FY27 total sales including Kesda about 5.5 lakh tons; EBITDA upward of INR550 crore. FY28 about 7 lakh tons and EBITDA upward of INR750 crore (volume and EBITDA targets as stated on the call).
Stainless steel Kesda plant (360,000 tpa, with 25 MW power) to be live by March 2027; first-year utilisation 30-35%, 60-65% by FY29.

Net debt to operating EBITDA expected to rise to about 1.4-1.5x during capex cycle; company aims to hold about 1.04x for full FY27.

Stainless steel operating at about 60% utilisation currently; mostly thinner-gauge output below 0.9 mm.
demand_pricing: Q2 MS pipe realisation about INR60-61; Q3 guided at INR63-64 as coil prices are elevated.
Q2 GP coil and pipe realisation about INR72-73; Q3 guided at INR78-79.
Stainless steel prices stable in Q3 per management, with 200 series price flat and 300 series price flat.
Chinese 200 and 300 series imports dumped below cost after QCO relaxation; management expects government action (minimum import price, anti-dumping) possibly by March 2027.
Seamless: domestic 2-3 lakh tpa documented demand; above 6-inch seamless about 90% imported; PLI 1.2 MoU signed with about 13% of revenue expected as incentive.
Stainless steel distributors and traders destocked in Q2 ahead of price rises; management said Q2 volume was partly pulled forward and Q3 volume will be capped at Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the EBITDA/ton fall from Q1 to Q2 came from mix versus price and cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the roughly INR600/ton fall to monsoon raw material yield losses, stainless steel margin compression of 12,000-13,000 tons per annum from QCO relaxation and Chinese dumping, and normalising Q1 war-driven price spikes. Q1 was described as an outlier.

qa_highlights.question: Is the seamless plant's EBITDA per ton and return on capital sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited 304 realisation of INR350-360/ton with INR50-55 margin and 316 realisation above INR450/ton with INR80-90 margin. It estimated about 15-16% normal EBITDA margin and INR60-70 crore EBITDA at about 10,000 tons; ROCE estimate was above 24-25%.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Kesda stainless expansion be sold at a discount to imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 10% PLI incentive lets it undercut prices and cited export premiums of 10-15% for competitors. It said first sales will be to replacement and trader markets that need no OEM approval, with OEM approvals expected within 1-2 years of production.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q2 operating performance continue into Q3 and Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the stainless steel margin of INR12,000-13,000/ton is sustainable with imports already in the market. It said Q3 capacity utilisation cannot rise above Q2, and volume is capped at Q1 levels because of distributor destocking.

qa_highlights.question: Are working capital days of 4-5 sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said the improvement reflected one-time destocking, faster customer recoveries and better supplier credit. She said 20-25 days is the optimum level for the company and the industry.

Raw material supply for stainless (nickel substitutes, imported high-value alloys, nickel pig iron) and Middle East-related shipping disruption, though management says supply is currently adequate.
Q3 volumes capped at Q1 levels after destocking and realisations guided up on elevated coil prices.

544439|2026-03.headline: Crizac FY26 revenue rose 22.7% to INR 10,422 mn and Q4 PAT rose 50% to INR 750 mn, but management withheld FY27 guidance until next quarter.

544439|2026-06.headline: Crizac Q1 FY27 revenue fell 4% YoY to INR2,012 million on adverse university mix; management now guides FY27 flat versus FY26.
544439|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations was INR2,012 million, down 4% YoY and below the INR3,917 million of Q4 FY26, consistent with Q1 being the seasonal trough. Management attributed the decline to a less favourable university mix (fewer high-fee top-ranked university bonuses and slabs), not lower platform activity, as enrolments rose 15% YoY. EBITDA fell 7.6% YoY to INR600 million, with margin at 29.8% versus 31%, while PAT grew 2.9% to INR471 million. Management moved from earlier growth expectations to a flat FY27 outlook, citing flight disruption and rupee volatility expected to hit Q2, with pent-up demand expected in Q3 and Q4. It also announced a leadership change: Chairman Christopher Nagle stepped down as UK CEO and became Non-Executive Chairman of the Indian holding company, with Eric Wijmenga taking UK and Europe operations.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 growth be 20-25% or 15-17% as earlier hinted?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Management now expects FY27 flat versus FY26, with pent-up demand in Q3 and Q4 offsetting Q1 and Q2 shortfalls.

qa_highlights.question: Why is standalone PBT above consolidated PBT in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Crizac India standalone recognised some payments as revenue; investments in Crizac UK and subsidiaries should pay off in Q3.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has only about 20% public float and SEBI rules do not allow a buyback at this level; the compliance team will look at the suggestion.

qa_highlights.question: Will the UK concentration fall, and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, the target is to get UK share below 60% within about three years, aided by Innova (Netherlands) and other markets, though policy shifts will slow this.

qa_highlights.question: Will value-added services become material?
qa_highlights.answer: Not initially; they could add 2-5% to EBITDA and 1-1.5% of revenue over the next couple of years, with ForeignAdmits accelerating this.

qa_highlights.answer: No. Management said the DRHP commits to a minimum 40% of PAT as dividend for at least three years; FY26 is done, leaving at least two more years.

544439|2026-09.headline: Crizac Q2 FY27 operating income fell 36.7% YoY to INR 1,027 million; management guides FY27 revenue and profit in line with FY26 on deferred students.
544439|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was hit by the West Asia conflict, currency moves in a key source market, and post-grad students deferring intakes. Operating income was INR 1,027 million (down 36.7% YoY), operating EBITDA INR 330 million (down 44%), and PAT INR 369 million (down 23.7%). Management attributes the shortfall to timing, saying revenue is deferred rather than lost, with Q3 FY27 revenue guided up 10-12% YoY and FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26. An interim dividend of INR 4 per share was declared, and the company reported net cash of about INR 5,984 million.

segments.name: UK (anchor market)
segments.commentary: Management says UK-sponsored study visas fell 20% between FY24 and FY26 while Crizac students grew 53%. Three universities accounted for 44% of revenue. The UK budget of 28 October proposed a 2-year graduate visa for high-compliance universities versus 18 months for others from January 2027; qualifying universities are yet to be defined.

segments.name: Non-UK destinations
segments.commentary: Non-UK destinations were about 9.5% of H1 applications versus 4.7% in H1 FY26, but contributed only 1.4% of revenue as of today. Management targets 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30.

FY27 revenue and profit guided in line with FY26, barring any black swan event; management says a large share of Q4 applications is already received and being processed.
Interim dividend INR 4 per share declared; total FY27 dividend including final expected at INR 8-10 per share.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guided at 25-26%, same as last year; salary cost expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term.
No FY28 guidance yet; management says it will be in a better position to guide next quarter. FY28 is subject to market reaction and US mid-term election outcomes.

capex_capacity: Over 600 institutional partners; relationships with the top 30 partners exceed 5 years.

Platform processed over 2 lakh applications from 92 countries; enrolment rate 12.8% on a rolling 12-month basis.
USD 2.5 million committed in March 2026 to in-house development of EduMentor, an AI-led student-university matching and mentorship platform.
Asset-light model: accommodation and student loans are distributed as a DSA for third parties; no real estate acquisition planned.
Medway Education (New Zealand) acquired at the start of FY27; New Zealand main intake is February, so revenue lands in Q4.
demand_pricing: Applications fell about 3% YoY in Q2, but revenue fell about 37%. Management attributes the gap to deferral timing, not lower revenue per student or mix.
Market share rose from 3.5% to 6% globally (FY24 to FY26). Share of Indian students rose from 9% to 13.9%, while visas to Indian students fell 22% over the same period.
Share of ex-India students rose from 1.5% to 3.7%.
Students deferred to the November and January intakes. Management says the Q2 shortfall should be recovered in Q3 and Q4.
Gross margin was about 54% in Q2 versus about 70% last year. Management says this reflects the H1 mix: 30% retained and 70% paid to the accounting partner, with full-year margin expected at 65-70%.
Management believes AI will not remove agents: universities still need counsellors for visa and process support, and inter-university competition favours platforms.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the Q2 revenue gap came from post-August deferrals, and what gives confidence deferrals will convert rather than cancel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management did not quantify deferrals by student count, since they span September, November and January intakes. It cited pipeline evidence (applications, deposits, visas) supporting 10-12% Q3 growth, and said many students have deferred to the January intake.

qa_highlights.question: Is the applications-to-revenue gap purely timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes. Management said it was mainly students deferring, all timing-related, with no change in revenue per student.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 M&A or capital deployment be pursued given the cash balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is actively looking at M&A but is cautious given geopolitical uncertainty. Criteria include synergies, founders, source and destination jurisdictions, revenue and EBITDA; the target is EBITDA-accretive at 10-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone results hold up while consolidated results fell, and was the INR 57 crore termination fee one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Standalone India books revenue on application processing, ahead of UK subsidiaries, which book on enrolment. The termination fee to Crizac Informatics UK (INR 57 crore vs INR 21.5 crore in FY25) was a one-time item that will not recur in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for employee cost and EBITDA margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost is largely fixed and rose with acquisitions and tech hiring. Salary cost is expected at 3-4% of revenue in the medium to long term, and steady-state EBITDA margin is 25-26%.

qa_highlights.question: Can the company diversify away from the UK, and when will non-UK revenue reach 10%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no date for 10% non-UK revenue. It expects 30% of revenue from outside the UK by FY30, citing New Zealand (via Medway), Netherlands, Europe and expected openings in Australia, Canada and the US.

544441|2026-03.headline: Meta Infotech FY26 revenue rose 23% to INR270 crore but PAT fell to INR11 crore; management targets 4x PAT by FY29 with no numeric guidance.
544441|2026-03.overview: FY26 was described as an investment year: revenue grew 23% YoY to INR270 crore and H2 revenue grew 72% YoY to INR60 crore, but EBITDA fell to INR18 crore (FY25: INR25 crore) and PAT fell to INR11 crore (FY25: INR14 crore). Management attributed the squeeze to new hires, geographic expansion, 12 new vendor onboardings, a Thales-owned Imperva transition that cut professional services revenue from about INR8.5 crore to INR2 crore, and a forex loss on a large contract. The company set an aspirational target of up to 4x PAT by FY29 from FY26 levels, without numeric revenue or margin guidance. Order book stood at INR506 crore as of May 2026, about 1.9x FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: FY26 services revenue was about INR36 crore versus INR35 crore in FY25, roughly 13% of total revenue; services contributed 75% of FY26 EBIT. Management targets at least 25% growth in services revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Product / trading
segments.commentary: Product business, including the large low-margin deal, carried H2 product EBIT loss versus about 8.2% product EBIT margin in H1 per an analyst's reading; management said it will decline product deals below 5-6% margin and target 9-10% going forward.

guidance_outlook: Aspirational target to grow PAT up to 4x from FY26 levels by FY29, described as a three-year plan starting FY27; no revenue or margin numbers given on compliance grounds.
PAT margin to rise above 10% from about 4% currently; management said ex the large low-margin order, PAT margin would already exceed 10%.
Services mix expected to rise from about 13% toward 25-30% of revenue over three years.

Contracts to be signed on a Spot+2 forex basis going forward to avoid INR-price variability.
capex_capacity: Headcount rose from 265 (Mar-25) to 309 (Mar-26); share of core technical staff increased from about 50% to 90%.

Offices now in Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai and Hyderabad; Pune expected in one to two months.
In-house paid training centres in Mumbai and Hyderabad (three-month programme) feed fresh hires; Jetking tie-up used for three-year-bond resources.
Dubai: three projects running, one a three-year contract; Gulf, Australia, APAC and US expansion planned.
demand_pricing: Order book INR506 crore as of May 2026 (about 1.9x FY26 revenue), management said to execute over about three years.
Large single contract above INR100 crore (vendor Zscaler) is recognised mainly in H1; management said it would not have taken this order at its margin given a choice, and it dilutes PAT margin.
Largest customer, a private bank, was about 50-55% of FY26 revenue per management; other customers mostly below INR10 crore each.
Forex: INR rate moved from about INR80-85 to INR88-89 per USD on the large deal, causing a loss of a couple of crore; management said this was a one-time item.
Vendor base expanded to about 10 vendors with 12 added in FY26 (8 focused); two more PS partner agreements expected to be signed.
India cybersecurity market cited at USD6-7 billion, growing 15-18% YoY (management estimate).

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it would check the H2 segment numbers; it stated a policy to avoid product deals below 5-6% margin and to target 9-10% product margins.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO Paresh Soni said it is timing: about INR20 crore of inventory at March, expected to sell in April; tax payments also weighed on operating cash flow.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said no extra funding is needed for growth; the IPO was not required for expansion, and it cited delayed billing from forex-linked contracts.

544441|2026-09.headline: H1 FY27 revenue fell 57% YoY to ₹39.5 crore as Meta Infotech exited low-margin product sales, while EBITDA margin rose to 8.7% and PAT to ₹4.9 crore.

Revenue from operations was ₹39.5 crore versus ₹91 crore in H1 FY26 (stated as "210 crore" in the transcript, which appears to be a transcription error), and rose sequentially from ₹59.9 crore in H2 FY26. EBITDA was ₹7.8 crore (margin 8.7% vs 7.5%), and PAT was ₹4.9 crore versus ₹10.4 crore a year earlier. Management said the investment phase (new vendors, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi, Gulf operations) is complete and that revenue conversion is the next step. The order book was ₹92.7 crore as of September 30.

544443|2026-03.headline: Travel Food Services Q4 system-wide sales grew 27.7% YoY to INR9 billion, while FY26 adjusted consolidated PAT rose 21.5% to INR4.5 billion on about 1% traffic growth.
544443|2026-03.overview: Management described FY26 as a disruption-heavy year (India-Pakistan conflict, aircraft crash-related schedule cuts, FDTL crew rest curbs, Middle East conflict from March 2026) in which TFS airport passenger traffic grew only 1.2%. Despite this, system-wide sales grew 25.4% to INR32.1 billion, driven by 9.4% like-for-like growth and 13.1% net contract gains. Q4 saw gross margin of 87.3% (85.6% after a one-time reclassification) and EBITDA up 38.3%, but PAT growth was held to about 15% by a INR212 million litigation provision and a weaker JV contribution. Trade receivables rose to about INR2.64 billion at year-end on EATS ramp-up, which management expects to normalise by H1 FY27.

segments.commentary: About 55% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth driven by throughput, menu engineering and value combos.

segments.name: Lounges
segments.commentary: About 41% of FY26 consolidated revenue; growth from premiumisation and dwell time. Kyra Lounge opened at Hong Kong International Airport and a Cochin lounge opened in the year.

segments.name: Management and other services
segments.commentary: About 4% of FY26 consolidated revenue.

Management expects FY27 passenger traffic growth of around 5%, per public reports, with Q1 FY27 still affected by the war-like situation.

Management said domestic traffic was robust while international traffic fell nearly double digits in March-April, especially at southern airports and Goa.
