544458|2026-09.headline: Shree Refrigerations H1 FY27 revenue rose about 84-85% YoY to roughly INR 100 crore, with EBITDA margin up to 13.5% from 11%; FY27 margin guided at about 22%.
544458|2026-09.overview: H1 FY27 revenue was roughly INR 100 crore, up about 84-85% YoY, and EBITDA margin improved to 13.5% from 11% despite commodity inflation. Management reiterated 40% revenue CAGR and about 22% annual EBITDA margin guidance, while H1 margins remain skewed low versus H2. Order book stood at about INR 198.6-200 crore at September, down from INR 270 crore at the start of the year, and operating cash flow was negative about INR 42 crore in H1. Management said the data centre opportunity is excluded from guidance and is expected to take 6-12 months to gain traction.

financial_highlights.change: Up about 84-85% YoY vs H1 FY26
Down from INR 270 crore at start of year
Up from INR 105 crore; about 250 days
Up from about 370 days after IPO-era improvement

segments.name: Refrigeration vertical (HVAC, AC plant, Ref plant)
segments.commentary: Management reports a single refrigeration vertical with no separate product segments; HVAC is a larger share than AC plant, and Ref plant is a very small share. Retrofit is the major business line, with defence spares a large component, alongside installation, commissioning and service.

segments.name: Non-defence / industrial
segments.commentary: Industrial chillers and test equipment are described as negligible today. A new wholly owned subsidiary for sub-zero chillers (Aquilon) targets chemical, food and pharma, with commercial operations expected from next financial year.

segments.name: Data centre (oil-free / magnetic-bearing chillers)
segments.commentary: No data centre orders yet; the Danfoss Turbocor-based offering is sourced from an Australian partner. Management expects traction in 6-12 months and excludes data centre revenue from FY27 and FY28 projections.

guidance_outlook: Revenue to grow at about 40% CAGR; management reaffirmed this for FY27 and beyond, noting the guidance excludes data centre revenue.
EBITDA margin about 22% at annual level for FY27; H1 at 13.5% implies a steep H2 ramp, which management attributes to higher H2 volumes and product mix.
Working capital days expected to fall to about 350 days (CEO) and receivable days to about 200 days (CFO) over time.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive by year-end FY27.
Order book expected to be healthy by year-end; management said orders will come in continuously rather than concentrated in Aug-Sep as last year.
Subsidy for the Karad unit 2 facility (Maharashtra D-class area) is not in projections and could add to margin.
capex_capacity: Unit 2 (Karad/Hanbarwadi) recently opened with about 50,000 sq ft in use; combined with unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) total manufacturing area about 70,000 sq ft.
Adjacent land of about 50,000 sq ft is already levelled, so a new shed can be built quickly if a new opportunity arises.
Management says current capacity is sufficient for guidance; no fresh equity needed unless a new opportunity emerges.
Unit 1 (about 20,000 sq ft) being converted into a full testing facility, including an ambient-controlled AC test room.
Small CapEx expected for the Aquilon sub-zero chiller initiative; a small manufacturing unit is being set up.
demand_pricing: Navy fleet support ship turnkey project is among about 10 live projects; management cites a large AC/HVAC/Ref plant order for the Indian Navy.

Management cites a market of about INR 2,750 crore over two years from naval ship approvals (about 1% share) and about INR 2,500 crore in non-naval shipbuilding (about 0.5% share), for an estimated INR 4,000-5,000 crore opportunity.
Next-generation corvette (NGC) orders reportedly cleared by CCS; management expects part of the orders to convert into firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28.
Eight orders are in the pipeline.
Imports reduced from about 30%+ to single digit in AC plants, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Why are H1 margins low again, and what H2 margin is needed to hit guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited commodity (copper, metals) inflation on fixed-price contracts, offset by strategic sourcing and higher inventory. H2 is seasonally stronger due to higher volumes absorbing overheads and product mix. Management said the 22% guidance is annual, not half-yearly, and skewness should fade over 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Why are receivable days high and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivable days fell from about 350 in FY25 to 250 at March 2026, were held at about 250 in H1 despite 84% growth, and should go to about 200. Management said there is no one-off and that shipyard milestone-based payments limit faster reduction.

qa_highlights.question: Why is operating cash flow negative and when does it turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed negative operating cash flow of about INR 42 crore to strategic sourcing, H2 deliveries and higher receivables. Management expects cash flow to turn positive by the end of FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data centre plan and are orders expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no data centre orders yet; the oil-free/magnetic-bearing technology is sourced from an Australian partner, with no manufacturing in India until volumes justify it. Traction is expected in 6-12 months and is excluded from FY27-28 projections.

qa_highlights.question: Can capacity support 40% growth and are new capex or funds needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Capacity is sufficient for current guidance. Land is levelled for a further shed if needed. Funding would be raised only if a new opportunity needs it; the additional working capital is to come mainly from internal accruals and some bank borrowing.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the depreciation method changed to straight line?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said straight-line depreciation better reflects asset use and was adopted in a year of heavy capex. No quantified impact was given on the call.

risks_watch: Commodity inflation (copper, metals) on fixed-price contracts could compress margins if strategic sourcing is insufficient.
Negative operating cash flow and rising receivables (INR 128 crore) and inventory (INR 80 crore); working capital days were about 400 against a target of about 350.
Order book fell from INR 270 crore to about INR 200 crore; the H2 order ramp is not yet visible.
Dependence on naval shipbuilding timelines and government budget or election-related delays were raised as questions; management disputed the risk.
Data centre traction is unproven and excluded from guidance; management acknowledged no orders yet.
ROCE currently about 14-15% per analyst; management says the same capital base should lift returns as growth is funded by working capital.
544458|2026-09.management_tone: Confident on growth and the naval pipeline, with repeated reassurance on the 40% CAGR and 22% margin guidance. Cautious and somewhat evasive on H1 margin gap, cash flow and the data centre timeline, relying on H2 skew and sector explanations. Several answers were unclear or deflected, notably on the criminal case question.
key_quotes: We are growing at a 40% CAGR rate and we will continue to grow at 40% CAGR rate, definitely.
Our component of INR 2.75 lakh-crore is approximately 1%, which is INR 2,750 crore, is for the next two years.

We feel that we are still about 6 to 8 months, maybe even about a year away for that kind of traction and therefore, we do not actually include data centre business revenues either into this financial year nor into our projections for the next year.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 EBITDA margin 13.5% vs 11% last year and FY27 guided at about 22% annual, which needs a steep H2 ramp from higher volumes and mix, though commodity inflation on fixed-price contracts is a drag.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says current capacity (about 70,000 sq ft combined after Unit 2 opened) is sufficient for the 40% CAGR guidance, with no new shed planned unless a new opportunity emerges.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 revenue about INR 100 crore, up 84-85% YoY, and management guides about 40% revenue CAGR, backed by a 198.6-200 crore order book and 8 pipeline orders, though the order book fell from INR 270 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation was not disclosed, and management says no fresh equity is needed and only small capex is planned (Unit 1 testing conversion, Aquilon unit), so no major capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated the 40% revenue CAGR and 22% EBITDA margin; with H1 margin at 13.5% and operating cash flow at negative INR 42 crore, there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 must lift margin from 13.5% to about 22% annual, the order book fell from INR 270 to about INR 200 crore, and receivable days (about 250) and working capital (about 400 days vs 350 target) remain stretched.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aquilon sub-zero chiller subsidiary has commercial operations expected from next financial year (FY28), and data centre offering traction is expected in 6-12 months, but neither is in guidance and no orders exist yet.

rows.label: Naval fleet and NGC corvette orders converting to firm orders
rows.why: Management expects part of the cleared next-generation corvette orders to convert to firm orders in FY27 and the rest in FY28, with about 10 live projects and 8 pipeline orders, though the order book has fallen to about INR 200 crore.

rows.label: Operating cash flow turns positive and receivable days fall
rows.why: H1 operating cash flow was negative INR 42 crore and receivable days were about 250; management targets positive cash flow by FY27 end and receivable days of 200 going forward, with shipyard milestone payments limiting pace.

rows.label: Karad unit 2 subsidy not in projections
rows.why: The Maharashtra D-class area subsidy for the Karad facility is excluded from projections and could add to margin, but no amount was quantified on the call.

tone.note: Management was confident on the 40% CAGR, naval pipeline and 22% margin guidance, but cautious and at times evasive on the H1 margin gap, negative cash flow and the data centre timeline, while analysts pressed on receivables, working capital and order book decline.

544459|2026-03.headline: Shanti Gold Q4 FY26 revenue rose 121.65% YoY to INR 658.93 crore, a record quarter, with EBITDA margin at 10.17%.
544459|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR 658.93 crore, up 121.65% YoY, the highest quarterly revenue in company history, driven by new customers, higher volumes and elevated gold prices. FY26 revenue reached INR 2,018.71 crore (+82.46%), with PAT of INR 140.15 crore (6.94% margin). Management changed inventory valuation from FIFO to weighted average cost with retrospective effect from April 1, 2024. Much of the profit uplift was attributed by management to inventory gains from gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, and management guided to a core PAT margin of around 4%.

financial_highlights.change: from INR 9.19 crore in Q4 FY25

segments.name: Studded / bridal jewellery (existing line)
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of revenue comes from the existing studded line; bridal jewellery carries higher margins and contributed to the Q4 EBITDA improvement.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery (new line)
segments.commentary: About 30% of revenue is from the newly entered machine-made plain gold segment, which management described as lower margin, higher volume.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance: volume growth of 30% to 40% and value growth of 60% to 70%; management cited FY27 turnover of around INR 3,000 to 3,500 crore in one answer and about INR 4,000 crore in another.

Core PAT margin guided at around 4% (management cited a 3.5% to 4% core range); the FY26 margin above this was attributed to inventory gains on gold bought outright with IPO proceeds, which management says is now mitigated and not included in guidance.
Export share guided to rise from about 5-10% to 10-20% this year, with Dubai subsidiary incorporation extended to June 2026.
Management expects to reach full 7,900 kg capacity in three to four years.
Working capital: management said inventory and trade receivables are each under 50 days; plain jewellery is expected to improve working capital cycle over time.
Debt-equity: management said it is comfortable at up to 1:1 (currently 0.36) to fund growth.
capex_capacity: Existing Andheri facility: installed capacity about 2,700 kg per annum, operating at around 65% utilisation.
Marol facility in Mumbai: adds about 4,000 kg per annum; management said it should be ready in about a month, starting at roughly 100 kg per month before ramping up.
Jaipur facility: adds 1,200 kg per annum; expected to start around September-October 2026.
Post-expansion total installed capacity is about 7,900 kg per annum, roughly three times the current capacity.
Quarterly volume reported at about 145-150 kg per month in a Q&A answer, which management said was disclosed quarterly in the presentation.
demand_pricing: Management said the structural shift from unorganised to organised jewellery retail is driving outsourcing to scalable manufacturers.

Management said demand is resilient, particularly in wedding and occasion-led categories; new products include Turkish jewellery (Turkish artisans onboarded for Marol), Mangalsutra and Cuban bracelets.
Management said the company has more than 400 customers and about 7% of volume or value from its top customer; it does not supply Titan/Tanishq currently.

Gold price context: management cited a move from about INR 78,000 to about INR 108,000 per 10 g and an assumed price of about INR 1,50,000 for guidance; it said guidance is based on current prices and not speculation.
Management said the 15% import duty increase would not hurt demand, citing a period when duty was 15% for many years and was cut to 6% last year.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY26 growth mainly price-driven, and what is the demand outlook ex-gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew about 15% in FY26 after the IPO and value growth was higher; FY27 is guided at 30-40% volume and 60-70% value growth.

qa_highlights.question: Sustainable margin and how much of FY26 profit was from gold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a core PAT margin of around 4% is sustainable; the extra profit came from gold bought outright with IPO money, when gold prices rose.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation and volume per month?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation is about 65%; volume is about 145-150 kg per month per the quarterly figures in the presentation.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and maximum debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said debt-equity of up to 1:1 is the target ceiling, with the current ratio at 0.36; inventory and receivables are each under 50 days.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volume guidance fall from 60-70% to 30-40%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 volume grew 15% and FY27 guidance of 40% plus is an increase, not a reduction; no contradiction in volume guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hedging policy and inventory held?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its hedging policy is to buy as it sells; it said about 600 kg of stock plus debtors is left, and it does not chase price movements.

risks_watch: Gold price volatility: management acknowledged gains and losses from inventory price movements; FY26 profit included inventory gains that management says are now excluded from guidance.
Margin gap: FY26 PAT margin was 6.94% versus the 4% core margin guided for FY27, and an analyst noted that doubling revenue to INR 4,000 crore at 4% implies only about INR 160 crore PAT.
Execution of the Marol (about 4,000 kg) and Jaipur (1,200 kg) ramp-ups, and the timing of the Jaipur start in September-October 2026.
Working capital and receivables: debtor days rose from 42 to 48-49; management expects new plain jewellery to improve the cycle.
Leverage: debt-equity expected to rise towards 1:1 to fund growth from 0.36 currently.
Geopolitical risk: the Dubai subsidiary has been delayed to June 2026 and export share targets depend on it.
Management said the 15% import duty would not hurt demand, but the duty increase is a demand-side watch item.
544459|2026-03.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand, but defensive and at times evasive on margin sustainability and gold-price exposure, repeatedly redirecting to a 4% core margin. Answers on the inventory gains and PAT trajectory were inconsistent, and the call was marked by answers that were brief and sometimes unclear.
key_quotes: Q4FY26, we achieved the highest ever quarterly revenues in the histo ry of the company, reflecting our strong execution capabilities, improving scales, and increased relevance as a trusted manufacturing partner for organized jewellers.
We are not speculating on the gold market price movement whether it goes North or South.
So our core margin, come what may, will always remain between in the range of 3.4% to 4%, which is the normal industry range.
Our hedging policy is quite simple. We buy as we sell. Simple.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guides core PAT margin of around 4% (3.5-4% range) for FY27 versus FY26 PAT margin of 6.94% that included inventory gains, and plain gold jewellery (about 30% of revenue) is described as lower margin, higher volume.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Marol ready in about a month (Q1 FY27); Jaipur 1,200 kg/yr s
rows.why: Marol adds about 4,000 kg/yr (148% of the existing 2,700 kg) and is in trial runs, with Jaipur 1,200 kg/yr (44%) under construction, taking installed capacity to about 7,900 kg/yr.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides 30-40% volume growth in FY27 backed by new capacity, against current utilisation of about 65% on 2,700 kg installed and volume of about 145-150 kg per month.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 65%, so there is no immediate pressure for new capex while Marol and Jaipur are still ramping; management says it is comfortable taking debt-equity up to 1:1 from 0.36 to fund growth, which leaves room for more capex later.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding conservatively on a 4% core PAT margin and says the FY26 excess came from inventory gains that are excluded from guidance; FY27 revenue guidance is also inconsistent (INR 3,000-3,500 crore vs about INR 4,000 crore), so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Ramp-up risk on Marol (starting at about 100 kg per month) and Jaipur timing (Sep-Oct 2026), plus gold price volatility, debtor days rising from 42 to 48-49, and the Dubai subsidiary already delayed to June 2026.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management has named new products (Turkish jewellery with artisans onboarded for Marol, Mangalsutra and Cuban bracelets) tied to the Marol ramp, and plain gold jewellery is already 30% of revenue.

rows.label: Export share rise and Dubai subsidiary
rows.why: Export share guided to rise from about 5-10% to 10-20% this year, but the Dubai subsidiary has already been extended to June 2026, so timing depends on it.

rows.label: Plain jewellery working capital improvement
rows.why: Inventory and receivables are each under 50 days, but debtor days rose from 42 to 48-49, and management expects plain jewellery to improve the cycle without a firm date.

rows.label: Customer base and wedding demand
rows.why: More than 400 customers, top customer only about 7% of volume or value, and management says wedding and occasion demand is resilient, supporting the 30-40% volume guide.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, capacity and demand, but defensive and evasive on margin sustainability and gold-price exposure, repeatedly pointing to the 4% core PAT margin; analysts pressed on how much FY26 profit came from inventory gains and on the inconsistent FY27 turnover figures.

544459|2026-06.headline: Shanti Gold Q1 FY27 revenue rose 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores, with PAT of INR50.48 crores, though management flagged about 2-2.5 points of EBITDA margin from one-off inventory gains.
544459|2026-06.overview: Revenue from operations grew 144.69% YoY to INR716.38 crores and PAT rose 46.94% to INR50.48 crores, with PAT margin at 7.05%. EBITDA was INR71.45 crores at a 9.97% margin, which management said includes roughly 2-2.5 percentage points of unrealised inventory gain from the FIFO-to-WAC change. Management guided to 7.5-8% EBITDA margin going forward, reiterated FY27 guidance of 50-60% value growth and 30-40% volume growth (about INR3,500 crores revenue), and said the Marol (Mumbai) plant commenced operations in June 2026. A INR100 crore rights issue was approved to fund working capital and growth.

financial_highlights.change: +144.69% YoY vs INR292.78 crores in Q1 FY26
+39% YoY vs INR51.41 crores in Q1 FY26
Management plans to take it up to below 1x

segments.name: Studded jewellery
segments.commentary: Management said about 70% of jewellery sold is studded; in a separate answer it said 75% of revenue is designer jewellery and 25% plain gold, and about 75% is cast-studded. The figures given during the call are inconsistent and need clarification.

segments.name: Plain gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Management cited about 30% of jewellery sold as plain gold, or 25% of revenue, in different answers.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Exports were 4% of Q1 revenue. A Dubai office is awaiting RBI approval; management described it as the base for international expansion, currently serving three to four countries.

guidance_outlook: FY27 value growth guidance of 50-60% YoY, equal to a revenue target of about INR3,500 crores; management said it could revise upward if Q3 demand is strong.
FY27 volume growth guidance of 30-40% YoY. Management called a repeat of the roughly 61-62% Q1 volume growth 'wishful thinking'.
Sustainable EBITDA margin of 7.5-8% for FY27 after removing the 2-2.5 point inventory gain; management said margin could move toward 10% over three to four years as new facilities scale.
Jaipur facility to start around mid-November or December 2026, with capex of about INR47 crores.
Management expects working capital needs to rise and plans a debt/equity mix that stays below 1x, funded by debt plus the INR100 crore rights issue.
capex_capacity: Marol (Mumbai) manufacturing facility began operations in June 2026, with a new 4,000 kg-capacity line that is ramping up; management said it is a different jewellery line from the existing plant.
Existing Mumbai plant capacity is about 2,700 kg and is running at about 75% utilisation.
Jaipur facility capex is about INR47 crores; first phase is 50,000 sq ft on a 3-acre site, expected to add about 1,200 kg. Operations are targeted for mid-November to December 2026.

544459|2026-09.headline: Shanti Gold's Q2 FY27 revenue rose 73.4% YoY to INR746 crores, but EBITDA margin compressed to about 5.7% as management reiterated FY27 revenue guidance of INR3,200-3,500 crores.

544465|2026-03.headline: Laxmi India Finance FY26 AUM rose over 27% to INR1,626 crore, PAT up 38% to INR49.7 crore, Gross NPA 2.13%.
544465|2026-03.overview: FY26 was the company's first year as a listed entity after its August 2025 IPO, with AUM of INR1,626 crore (on-book INR1,519 crore) and disbursements of INR821 crore. Net interest income rose nearly 39% to INR161 crore and PAT rose over 38% to INR49.7 crore. Blended cost of borrowing fell to 10.8% from 11.48%, and Acuite upgraded the rating to A/Stable. Management guided to 30-35% AUM CAGR and about 40-45% PAT growth in FY27, with Q4 PAT helped by an upfront gain of INR8.66 crore on a INR41 crore direct assignment (DA) pool.

segments.name: Secured MSME and retail lending
segments.commentary: Portfolio is about 98% secured, with 37% of borrowers first-time borrowers and mostly assessed-income customers. Rajasthan accounts for about 82% of AUM, MP about 11% and Gujarat about 7%.

segments.name: Branch network
segments.commentary: 176 branches across six states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, Chhattisgarh, UP, Maharashtra), with 18 added in FY26. Breakeven takes about 7-8 months and about INR1.5-2 crore of disbursement per branch.

segments.name: Treasury / borrowings
segments.commentary: Over 40 lenders across PSU banks, private banks, SFBs, NBFCs and FIs; bank borrowings are the focus. Incremental cost is about 10.25-10.30%, and post-IPO fresh borrowing is at 10-10.25%.

PAT growth of around 40-45% expected in the current year (FY27).

Management said existing branches (including 18 added in FY26) have matured enough to deliver much of the 30-35% growth without new branches.
Agreement e-signing is still manual/physical; electronic signing is planned shortly, with the rest of the underwriting workflow already digital.
demand_pricing: Management says banks and fintechs largely avoid non-income-proof customers, which the company targets through field income verification.
Yield has been stable over the last 3-4 years; NIM is expected to hold at current levels or rise as cost of funds falls.
Q4 NIM and revenue were lifted by an INR8.66 crore upfront gain on a INR41 crore DA pool sale.
Management sees little stress from oil and energy prices, citing rural cash-flow borrowers and a vehicle portfolio of only 9%; it conceded some slowdown is possible if oil prices stay high.

544466|2026-03.headline: Aditya Infotech Q4 FY26 revenue rose 45.5% YoY to INR1,422 crore with EBITDA margin of 18%; FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR6,000-6,500 crore.

qa_highlights.answer: Anup Nair said the cash conversion cycle has risen because creditors fell as the company secured supply, and some inventory is being blocked with advance payments. Working capital is factored into FY27 plans; capex is to be funded mainly from internal accruals and some debt.

qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Khemka said the earlier plan of about INR200 crore has been raised to INR200-300 crore for FY27, with FY28 plans still under work. Funding is through internal accruals and some debt; the debt-equity ratio is very low.

544471|2026-03.headline: H2 FY26 revenue fell to Rs 28.97 crore with 5.32% EBITDA margin as management deferred loss-making fixed-price contracts amid component inflation.
544471|2026-03.overview: Takyon reported H2 FY26 (Oct 2025 to Mar 2026) consolidated revenue of Rs 28.97 crore, EBITDA of Rs 1.61 crore (5.32% margin) and PAT of Rs 0.44 crore. Full-year FY26 revenue was Rs 71.05 crore, EBITDA Rs 7.09 crore (near 10%), PAT Rs 3.65 crore and EPS Rs 3.29. H1 FY26 revenue was Rs 42.08 crore with EBITDA margin near 13%. Management attributed the H2 shortfall to component price inflation and lengthened lead times, and said it chose to defer unviable fixed-price contracts and protect the balance sheet. Total liabilities fell from Rs 50 crore to Rs 12.20 crore and trade payables from Rs 30.21 crore to Rs 3.77 crore.

544479|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR145.8 crore (from INR148.2 crore) on West Asia disruptions, while gross margin rose to 41.9% and EBITDA margin was 14.8%.
544479|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue declined year-on-year as late-March supply and port disruptions linked to the West Asia crisis pushed shipments into April, with management citing a 10-15% shift in volumes. Gross margin improved to 41.9% on a better product, customer and export/domestic mix, and EBITDA was INR21.6 crore (14.8%) with PAT of INR9.4 crore (6.4%). For FY26 revenue grew 9.4% to INR610.4 crore, but EBITDA margin compressed to 14.8% and PAT fell to INR35.6 crore from INR47.3 crore as new Khatalwada capacity and employee costs weighed. Management expects FY27 margins to be better than FY26 with H2 improvement, but Q1 faces a temporary margin hit as price increases of 20-25% are only partly accepted by customers (10-12%).

544479|2026-09.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 18% YoY to INR174 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 7.9% as raw material cost pass-through lagged.
544479|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was a margin-compressed quarter: revenue grew 18% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR174 crore, while gross margin fell to 34.3% and EBITDA margin to 7.9%. Management attributed this to a fresh input-cost spike from the West Asia conflict, export orders priced before the spike, and a deliberate choice to absorb part of the cost increase for long-standing customers. Working capital rose sharply, inventory to INR120.2 crore and receivables to INR100.1 crore, and H1 operating cash flow was negative. Management says the shipment backlog and receivables are unwinding into Q3 and guides to 15-20% FY27 revenue growth and 7-8% volume growth.

segments.commentary: Domestic revenue grew about 36% QoQ and 27% YoY, lifting its share to 19.5% from 15.5% in Q1. 36 new customers were added in H1 and a new Hydration range of bottles and jars was launched. Management says domestic gross margin is 12-13 points above export.

segments.name: Exports - United States
segments.commentary: US contributed about 10% of revenue in Q2 versus about 19% in Q1, which management attributes to shipment timing. A US stationery customer is expected to roughly double business as products move into its core range, and to become the second-largest customer by end-FY27.

segments.name: Exports - European Union and UK
segments.commentary: EU contributed about 59% of revenue and UK about 10%. Largest customer contribution was 59% per the Q&A. October sales were described as encouraging.

segments.name: Bamboo (subsidiary All Time Bamboo Pvt Ltd, Guwahati)
segments.commentary: Guwahati facility is fully installed, with commercial production from mid-November 2026 and revenue expected from Q4 FY27. Management guides about INR60 crore revenue at current installed capacity, and separately INR25-30 crore for CY27. Total capex to date about INR18 crore, targeted at INR20 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of 15-20%, with management reiterating it on the call.
FY27 volume (production) growth of at least 7-8%, with at least 15,000 MT production targeted in H2 FY27 on the current order book.
Capacity utilisation will not reach 75% in Q4 FY27; management targets 75% by Q2 FY28.

Gross margin and EBITDA expected to improve in H2 as price increases are negotiated and fixed costs at Khatalwada and Bamboo are absorbed. Management said margins could be better than the 12-13% EBITDA range discussed if conditions normalise.
Domestic growth target of 30-35% retained.
About INR8 crore sales-in-transit and roughly 500 MT of Q2 sales (per the Q&A) are expected to be recognised in Q3 FY27, along with the production of extra finished goods.
Working capital expected to unwind in H2 and operating cash flow to turn positive.
Bamboo facility expected to double, with about INR10-12 crore of additional machinery, once utilisation reaches about 50%; management said this could happen by end-FY28.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is about 41,000 tonnes currently. 14 injection moulding machines adding about 1,500 tonnes are expected in December 2026, taking capacity to about 42,500 MT, which management calls the peak for now.

Blow-moulding capability has been added within the existing plant for bottles and jars in PP, PET, PETg and Tritan, scalable with demand. SCADA-based real-time machine monitoring has been initiated at Khatalwada.

Further capex will be project-by-project for confirmed programmes. Bamboo commercial production starts mid-November 2026; split-processing model has boards made at Guwahati and value-add at Khatalwada.
Silvassa production was suspended for 3 days in September due to storage constraints.
demand_pricing: Average polymer prices rose 40-45%. Export prices are fixed at order and revisable only on new orders, so confirmed orders were honoured at agreed prices.
About 50% of the input-cost increase has been passed to non-IKEA/non-largest customers so far. Domestic price increase was to be rolled out from the second week of November.
Management said some customers are resisting price increases because they are benchmarking against Chinese prices.
Management flagged possible demand headwinds at higher price points for some articles, but said utilisation has improved and no dramatic demand fall is visible.
Container backlog for the largest customer fell from 126 to 32 40-foot containers. Inbound raw material transit rose to about 50 days from a historic 30 days.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR120 crore inventory is finished goods, and how much will be recognised in Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Finished goods were INR42 crore at end-Q2, of which INR8 crore is sales-in-transit recognised in October. The INR15.4 crore change in inventory includes INR8 crore sales to be booked in October and INR7 crore of extra production.

qa_highlights.question: How will gross margin trend, and what is the domestic vs export margin gap?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins should rise once raw material prices fall or prices are renegotiated; domestic price increases are in process. The gross margin gap between domestic and export is about 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q3 see better gross margin than Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects some pricing gains in Q3 and Q4, but not back to historical levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 volume outlook, and is H2 visibility strong?
qa_highlights.answer: At least 7-8% volume growth for FY27. Management says H2 visibility is strong, with at least 15,000 MT production targeted in H2 on the current order book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bamboo ramp slower than planned, and is there demand headwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described Bamboo as a discovery phase; Guwahati is ready, with European sales waiting on FSC certification over a few months. Management said there is no dramatic demand fall, but price-sensitive articles could see some headwinds.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cost increase has been passed on, and will falling crude be a margin benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: About 50% of the 40-45% increase has been passed to most customers, with the largest customer and IKEA on rollover contracts. Management says customers have committed to recover lost margins as prices fall.

risks_watch: Gross margin recovery depends on customer price renegotiations, with about half the raw-material cost increase passed through so far and some customers pushing back against Chinese pricing.
Working capital: inventory of INR120.2 crore and receivables of INR100.1 crore must unwind in H2 for operating cash flow to turn positive; H1 operating cash flow was negative.
Shipping and container disruption: inbound transit around 50 days versus a historic 30 days, and the container backlog must clear as stated.
Fixed-cost absorption at Khatalwada and Bamboo, and whether utilisation moves from 67% toward the 75% target by Q2 FY28.
Concentration: largest customer contributed 59% of revenue, and US share fell to about 10%.
544479|2026-09.management_tone: Candid and cautious on near-term margins, attributing the miss to external shocks and a deliberate choice to absorb costs; confident on H2 volume, order visibility and the long-term domestic and Bamboo story. Answers on Bamboo capex and demand headwinds were qualified, and management avoided firm timelines on price recovery.

The increase in working capital is temporary, and our inventory carries no slow-moving stocks.
We have consciously absorbed part of this cost increase to protect the long -standing customer relationships.
We expect a substantial portion of the working capital buildup to unwind during H2 as the shipment backlog clears and collections are realized.
So the EBITDA margin will definitely be much better in H2.
Second half visibility is very strong. Orders are also there.

544480|2026-03.headline: JSW Cement Q4 FY26 operating EBITDA rose 46% YoY to INR365 crore (19.3% margin), helped by a one-time INR211 crore deferred tax benefit lifting PAT to INR362 crore.
544480|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 11% YoY to INR1,895 crore on 3.99 million tons of sales volume (+7%), with cement realisation up 4.8% QoQ to INR4,673/ton. Operating EBITDA reached INR916/ton, but GGBS volumes grew only 5.4% YoY due to a slag supply disruption at Dolvi and RMC site closures in Western India. The Nagaur (Rajasthan) plant began commercial operations on 30 March 2026, and management trimmed the Punjab plan in favour of a 2.5 MTPA grinding unit at Nagaur. April demand was soft, though management says volumes are recovering from mid-May.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth guided at mid-to-high teens, excluding the North plant; management says it is on track.

Capex guided at about INR2,300 crore in FY27 and INR2,200 crore in FY28; about INR2,400 crore already spent at Nagaur against a total of about INR3,500 crore including the additional 1 MTPA grinding unit.

Cost savings programme: over 50% of target achieved; about INR100/ton more expected in FY27 and the balance in FY28 (power about INR69-70/ton, logistics about INR36/ton, premiumisation about INR4/ton for cement).

Nagaur grinding capacity to rise to 3.5 MTPA shortly, and to 6 MTPA after a new 2.5 MTPA unit (INR430 crore, commissioning by Q4 FY28). Company-wide grinding target of 46 MTPA and clinker of 13.04 MTPA; FY30 capacity target of about 43.5 MTPA intact.
FY27 tax rate assumed at 25% under the new regime; Rajasthan state capital subsidy of about INR50 crore plus electricity duty waiver expected.
GGBS volume guidance of about 6.5-7 million tons for FY27 maintained.
UAE grinding unit delayed about one month by the war; commissioning now expected by end-April 2027.

demand_pricing: Q4 industry growth in company markets 8% YoY versus company cement volume +12%, implying share gains.

Western India RMC closures from pollution concerns (Mumbai, then Pune to end-April) are now resolved, per management.

Cement realisations rose across all regions in Q4; GGBS realisation roughly flat QoQ. Management says no windfall from steel price rises because slag is contract-priced (5-year contract from October 2024, price review every 2.5 years).

Premium product share about 52% of volume in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the industry demand outlook and the growth of JSW Cement in the new northern region?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 volume growth is guided at mid-to-high teens excluding the North; April was soft but May is normalising.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex guidance and spend at Nagaur to date?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR2,300 crore and FY28 about INR2,200 crore; INR2,400 crore already spent at Nagaur against a total of about INR3,500 crore including the additional 1 MTPA grinding.

qa_highlights.question: Why was INR23 crore of North spend not capitalised, and is it one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said branding and promotion spend cannot be capitalised under its accounting policy; it is a recurring cost, as hoardings need replacing every 2-3 years.

qa_highlights.question: Where will clinker for Punjab come from, and what is the impact of the Punjab delay?
qa_highlights.answer: Punjab EC is delayed beyond FY28. Nagaur clinker (3.3 MTPA) is fully used by the 6 MTPA grinding plan, so a second Rajasthan kiln line will be considered once EC is in place.

qa_highlights.question: How much cost saving is realised, and what remains?
qa_highlights.answer: Over 50% of the INR400/ton programme has been achieved; around INR100/ton is expected in FY27 and the balance in FY28, at company level about INR50-75/ton each year.

qa_highlights.question: Will GGBS prices benefit from higher steel prices, and is the UAE unit supply sufficient?
qa_highlights.answer: No windfall expected since slag is contract-priced and freight from China is high. Clinker for Dolvi is secured until December at pre-war fixed prices; the JV sells about 1.5 million tons to the UAE grinding unit.

risks_watch: West Asia conflict: higher packing, imported fuel and petrol/diesel costs, and inflation affecting near-term demand.
Dolvi slag availability and the Western region RMC/pollution disruption, which affected GGBS in Q4; watch Q1 FY27 GGBS volume recovery.
Punjab EC delay (elections due February 2027) and the timing of a second Rajasthan kiln line.
Nagaur ramp-up: first month of operations; management will update on utilisation at end-Q1 against the 50-60% full-year guidance.
Ongoing rupee depreciation (INR13.4 crore hit in Q4) and the April-May demand softness.
Cost savings delivery: about INR100/ton still to come in FY27.

544480|2026-06.headline: JSW Cement Q1 FY27 volume rose 15% YoY to 3.81 Mt, but consolidated operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore on North start-up costs and fuel.
544480|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 volumes grew 15% YoY to 3.81 million tons, with cement up 27% to 2.34 Mt; ex-North cement volume grew 8%. Consolidated revenue was INR1,896 crore (+22% YoY, flat QoQ) while operating EBITDA fell 7.5% YoY to INR299 crore (INR784/t), as blended fuel cost rose to INR1.80/Mcal from INR1.49 and North marketing spend was about INR33 crore. Management kept high-teens company-wide volume growth guidance for FY27 but cut GGBS growth expectations to high single digits. North breakeven is targeted at EBITDA level in Q2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was GGBS growth slow and what growth is expected?

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling company-wide high-teens volume growth with ex-North growth of 8% and GGBS high single digits.

Management said pre-Ind AS EBITDA margins improved YoY despite a mix shift toward plain gold, and attributed the recovery to rapid entry-level repricing and vertical integration. Gold price inflation inflated closing inventory, which pushed inventory turns down to about 1.13x from 1.3x in FY25.

544484|2026-06.headline: BlueStone Q1 FY27 revenue rose 49% YoY to INR 733 crore, with pre-Ind AS EBITDA up 135% to INR 55 crore and margin at 7.5%.
544484|2026-06.overview: Revenue grew 49% YoY to INR 733 crore and pre-Ind AS EBITDA rose 135% to INR 55 crore, lifting operating margin to 7.5% (up 273 bps). Management attributed this to operating leverage despite a custom duty hike on gold from 6% to 15% that softened demand in May before June and July recovered. Same-store sales growth was 39%, repeat revenue share rose to about 60%, while new customer additions reportedly fell from about 50,000 to about 40,000 per quarter, which management tied to merchandise dislocation during the sharp gold rise. Management reiterated a long-term target of roughly INR 12,000 crore revenue in four years, around 30% SSSG and about 20% store distribution growth, though analysts questioned the arithmetic.

544484|2026-09.headline: BlueStone Q2 FY27 revenue grew 44% YoY to INR 738 crore, EBITDA more than doubled, and the company posted its fourth consecutive standalone profitable quarter.
544484|2026-09.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 738 crore, up 44% YoY, with EBITDA more than doubling and a fourth straight profitable quarter on a standalone basis. Management said about 29% of the 44% growth came from AOV increase, with the rest from buyer growth, and that SSSG was around 28% in the quarter. The company crossed 1 million customers, opened 27 stores across 7 new cities, and reset entry-level price points, which lowered sequential AOV. Management said festive-season timing shifted some demand into Q3, and that early Q3 trends were in line with expectations, with most big buying days still ahead.

544485|2026-03.headline: Regaal FY26 operating income rose 23.9% to INR 1,134.2 crore and PAT reached INR 55.6 crore; 1,650 TPD expansion commissioned 26 May 2026, with no formal guidance until H1 FY27.
544485|2026-03.overview: FY26 showed strong growth, with operating income up 23.9% YoY to INR 1,134.2 crore, value-added revenue up 18% to INR 295.8 crore, and PAT of INR 55.6 crore (4.9% margin). Q4 FY26 operating income was INR 244.6 crore, operating EBITDA INR 32.5 crore (13.3% margin) and PAT INR 16.5 crore. Crushing capacity was raised to 1,650 TPD on 26 May 2026 with liquid glucose, maltodextrin and a 10 MW power addition, and the capex estimate rose from about INR 430 crore to INR 540 crore. Management declined to give FY27 volume, margin or revenue guidance, promising a firm outlook by end of Q1/H1 FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade

544485|2026-06.headline: Regaal Q1 FY27 operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr as trading was cut, while value-added margin rose to 39.8% and PAT grew 47% to Rs 13.33 cr.
544485|2026-06.overview: Q1 FY27 was a transition quarter: the doubled crushing capacity (825 to 1,650 TPD) was commissioned on 26 May 2026, with operations ramping from early June. Operating income fell 18% YoY to Rs 202.15 cr because low-margin trading was deliberately reduced (3.3% of revenue vs 19.5% in Q1 FY26). Value-added revenue grew 30.3% to Rs 80.53 cr and EBITDA rose 26.6% to Rs 30.98 cr, with margin up 540 bps to 15.3%. Capacity utilisation was 71.4%, with management guiding to progressive improvement from Q2 FY27 and a shift to deleveraging after the capex cycle.

segments.name: Trading
segments.commentary: Contribution fell to 3.3% of revenue in Q1 FY27 from 19.5% in Q1 FY26 as low-margin trading was deliberately cut.

segments.name: Value-added products (liquid glucose, maltodextrin, starches)
segments.commentary: Value-added revenue Rs 80.53 cr (+30.3% YoY) at 39.8% margin. Liquid glucose at about 70% of its capacity; maltodextrin powder still ramping, with 2-3 more months needed to reach target.

segments.name: Maize starch / core crushing
segments.commentary: Crushing of 69,689 MT in Q1, with about 5,500 MT of incremental volume attributed by management to liquid glucose and a small part maltodextrin.

guidance_outlook: FY27 crushing expected at about 4 lakh tons (minimum), vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.
Q2 FY27 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons, contingent on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Value-added share of turnover expected at about 20-22% in FY27 (vs about 3% last year); later guided to about 30-35% of turnover on capacity mix.
Management declined to give EBITDA per ton or EBITDA margin guidance, citing maize and product price dependence; said operating leverage and value-add mix should improve margins at constant prices.
Net interest cost (net of subvention) for FY27 expected at about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26.
Total project outlay about Rs 664 crore, of which about Rs 552 crore incurred as of 30 June 2026.
Working capital debt expected to decline in H2; management cited a prior pattern of about 40% reduction by Q4.
Dextrose Anhydrous, Dextrose Monohydrate and Hydrol expected by about Q4 FY27; modified starches (cationic, carboxymethyl, pre-gel, spray) trials to be fully online by September 2026.
No new capex decided; management said focus is on stabilising at 90-95% utilisation and deleveraging before considering next expansion.
capex_capacity: Crushing capacity doubled from 825 to 1,650 MT per day, commissioned 26 May 2026; operations started early June; described as largest maize wet milling facility in eastern India.
New liquid glucose facility 180 TPD, maltodextrin powder facility 50 TPD, captive cogeneration expanded from 7.1 MW to 15.8 MW.
Q1 utilisation 71.4%; about 9 shutdown days during April-May integration cost roughly 7,200 MT of output (management estimate).
Planned additions: 50,000 MT storage across two new silos, a 50,000 sq ft maize godown, and a 1.6 MW methane gas-based power plant.
Bihar interest subvention applies to new capex debt; management said the subvention cap was amended to Rs 40 crore but final policy notification was still awaited.
demand_pricing: Management said export share rose to 10.4% and that new markets in South and West India are being developed; no export target given.
Pricing: management said starch margin is a whole-number (per-ton) business rather than percentage-based; a rise in starch prices would not proportionally lift EBITDA per ton.
Maize procurement: about 80% of annual requirement bought in the Rabi season (Apr-Jul), 10-15% from other states; Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg delivered vs market talk of Rs 24.
Liquid glucose sold mainly September to March; big MNC customers now billed directly, and white-labelling customer base has grown.
About 70-80% of new modified starch volumes expected to go to existing paper-mill and food customers.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is the expanded plant running at and when will it reach a comfortable run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said utilisation is rising from the early-June start and expects maximum utilisation within the year; FY27 crushing expected above 4 lakh tons vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 47% PAT jump driven by raw material cost or operating leverage?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to operating leverage and the drop in low-margin trading from about 19% to about 3% of turnover.

qa_highlights.question: What sustainable EBITDA per ton should be expected in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to guide, citing maize and product price dependence; it expects per-ton EBITDA to improve with scale and value-add at constant prices (Q1 EBITDA/ton cited as about Rs 4,450 vs Rs 4,742 FY26).

qa_highlights.question: What is the net interest cost for FY27 after Bihar subvention?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about Rs 39-40 crore, broadly flat vs FY26; subvention runs across multiple project loans, with the Rs 40 crore cap still pending final policy.

qa_highlights.question: When will peak debt occur and when will working capital come down?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said debt is peaking in H1 FY27 because working capital is highest then; debt expected to fall in H2.

qa_highlights.question: What production was lost in Q1 and is the value-added capacity stable?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 shutdown days (approx. 7,200 MT lost). Liquid glucose at about 70% of capacity; maltodextrin needs 2-3 more months; modified starch trials to be online by September.

qa_highlights.question: Any new capex plans for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: No; management wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation and reduce debt before considering the next expansion.

risks_watch: Ramp-up risk: Q1 utilisation was 71.4% after about 9 shutdown days (about 7,200 MT lost); Q2 crushing guided to 100,000-110,000 tons and FY27 to at least 4 lakh tons, and both depend on smooth stabilisation and integration.
Maltodextrin powder still needs 2-3 more months to reach target; modified starch trials are to be fully online by September 2026 and dextrose products are expected by about Q4 FY27.
Working capital and leverage: cash conversion cycle at 130 days, net debt Rs 735.32 crore, and debt expected to peak in H1 FY27 before falling in H2.

Interest subvention: the Bihar subvention cap was reportedly amended to Rs 40 crore, but the final policy notification was still awaited; the Rs 20 crore cap is still the one being applied in accounts.
Margin visibility: management declined to guide EBITDA per ton or margin, citing maize and product price dependence, so FY27 margin trajectory remains unquantified.
Maize price exposure: Bihar maize quoted at about Rs 22.5-23/kg versus market talk of Rs 24, with about 80% of annual requirement already bought in the Rabi season.
key_quotes: Q1 FY’27 was a quarter of transition.
So, what we can definitely guide is that we are going to grow our production and we will get operating leverage.
Sustainable at the moment, I cannot tell you, because we are at a time of transition.
It’s too early for us to talk about another next expansion. We are just stabilizing this one.

Specific figures were given on crushing volumes, net interest cost and value-added share, while several answers (subvention amount, starch price trend, product margins) were deferred to the IR team.

rows.why: FY27 crushing guided at 4 lakh tons minimum vs about 2.65 lakh tons in FY26 (+50%), Q2 guided at 100,000-110,000 tons vs 69,689 MT in Q1, though contingent on stabilisation.

rows.why: Management said no new capex decided and wants to stabilise at 90-95% utilisation (Q1 at 71.4%) and deleverage (net debt Rs 735.32 cr) before the next expansion; only planned additions are silos, godown and 1.6 MW methane plant already in plan.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 PAT up 47% to Rs 13.33 cr and export share up to 10.4% from 4.9%, but management gave no revenue or margin upgrade and Q1 operating income fell 18%.

rows.why: Ramp-up risk: 9 shutdown days cost about 7,200 MT, Q1 utilisation 71.4%, maltodextrin still 2-3 months from target, and maize at Rs 22.5-23/kg vs Rs 24 market talk; Q2 guidance depends on smooth stabilisation.

rows.label: Working capital and debt peak then decline
rows.why: CFO said debt peaks in H1 FY27 as working capital is highest, with working capital debt expected to fall in H2 (management cited a prior ~40% reduction by Q4); net debt is Rs 735.32 cr and CCC is 130 days.

rows.why: Subvention cap reportedly amended to Rs 40 cr but final notification awaited; accounts still apply Rs 20 cr cap; FY27 net interest guided at Rs 39-40 cr, flat vs FY26.

rows.why: Export share of revenue rose to 10.4% from 4.9% in Q1 FY26, and management says new markets in South and West India are being developed, though no export target was given.

544487|2026-03.headline: Patel Retail Q4 FY26 PAT rose 39.07% YoY to INR9.98 crore on 53.35% higher income, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.70% as new-store costs hit.
544487|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 53.35% YoY to INR339.55 crore, with EBITDA up 31.21% to INR22.74 crore and PAT up 39.07% to INR9.98 crore. FY26 total income crossed INR1,000 crore at INR1,059.29 crore (+28.25%), with PAT up 54.48% to INR39.05 crore and PAT margin at 3.69%. Management attributed the weak Q4 EBITDA margin to upfront costs of new stores and said revenue ramp-up would come in FY27. Analyst questions focused on falling same-store sales (~5%), gross margin compression, a sizeable other-income (FX gain) contribution, and inventory and receivables build-up; several answers were incomplete or inconsistent.

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: 51 stores after Rasayani opening in April 2026 (over 2.29 lakh sq ft); 50th store at Thakurli in Q4. Retail sales INR429 crore in FY26; management cited retail EBITDA margin of 7-8% and gross margin of 14-15%, and retail contributes about 35-38% of PAT excluding other income.

segments.name: Manufacturing and processing (B2B)
segments.commentary: Ambernath and Kutch capacity over 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55% vs 45-48% earlier. Management cited about INR618 crore manufacturing and processing sales in FY26, of which about INR319 crore exports; gross margin guided at 16-17% (FY27: 18-20%). Management put manufacturing EBITDA margin at roughly 6.5-7%.

segments.name: Private label / own brands
segments.commentary: Own brands (Indian Chaska, Patel Fresh, Blue Nation, Patel Essentials) are about 17.5% of retail sales; own brands reportedly carry 30-35% operating margins per management, with non-branded gross margin of 15-16%. Indian Chaska distribution covers six states, with MP and Delhi in progress.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at approximately 8-9%.
Gross margin guided at 15-20% overall; FY27 mix expected at 18-20% for B2B and 15-16% for retail.
Management expects double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with 'higher side' at 20% and above, but declined to disclose numbers formally.
Plans to open 8-10 stores a year, with focus on western suburbs and PCMC; possible Gujarat entry. Management said 52 stores as of the call date and seven or eight more expected in FY27.
Management expects positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 as inventory normalises.
Management expects PAT margin to increase, and expects manufacturing utilisation to rise.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity at Ambernath and Kutch exceeds 1.47 lakh MTPA; utilisation 50-55%, up 4-5 percentage points.
Retail network 51 stores, over 2.29 lakh sq ft; management carries about INR2,000-2,500 inventory per sq ft at store level.
Distribution centre in the cluster holds an additional INR15-20 crore of inventory per management.
Plans to start whole spices in the month of the call, then seasonings, pastes, snacks, and noodles or pasta depending on distribution.
Automation investment planned to improve productivity and cost efficiency.
demand_pricing: Same-store sales growth around 5%; management said mature stores grow 5-6%, versus analyst's recollection of 8-10%.
Grocery and staples are about 68-70% of retail revenue.
Export order book held at INR50-100 crore per management; current export order book figure not provided on the call.
Exports to Sri Lanka, Middle East, Europe, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, with African markets being pursued; management says 35+ countries.
Other income of about INR5 crore in Q4 is mainly FX gain on export receivables; management said INR8-9 crore per year is typical and expected to keep rising.
Management said commodity prices have peaked and are declining, and expects inventory gains from raw material procured at competitive prices.

qa_highlights.question: Why did same-store sales appear to slow from 8-10% to about 5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 5% is good for mature stores, cited no specific reason, and said most revenue comes from grocery and staples (68-70%).

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory and working capital rise so much?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said incremental working capital was funded from IPO proceeds (INR115 crore deployed into working capital). Management also cited export order book, transit times, and mixed shipments; the exact export order book was not disclosed on the call.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 margin decline and gross margin fall from about 20% to 14.5%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed Q4 margin pressure to upfront costs of new stores, and said it is temporary. He did not separately quantify the gross margin decline; management said the West Asia situation had not been the primary factor.

qa_highlights.question: What is the nature of the other income and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said other income is mainly FX gain on export receivables, about INR8-9 crore a year, and expected to keep rising. Management did not explain why the Q4 figure was about INR5 crore or why the gain would be recurring.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail inventory at about INR90 crore, above the INR55-58 crore implied by store-level inventory per sq ft?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference reflects a cluster distribution centre (INR15-20 crore) and category-level inventory days, including about three months of spices stock and three to four months for plastic and steel, with festive stock also included.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise from INR125 crore to INR161-162 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about 90% of receivables are less than six months old. He did not explain the increase.

risks_watch: Same-store sales growth of about 5% versus the 8-10% the analyst cited previously; management did not give a clear reason for the slowdown.
Gross margin fell sharply in Q4 (analyst cited about 14.5% versus about 20% a year earlier); management has not quantified the cause.
Other income (FX gain) of about INR5 crore in Q4 is a large share of PAT growth; the analyst argued that excluding it would show a decline.
Inventory (INR259-260 crore) and receivables (INR161-162 crore) rose sharply; management guided to positive operating cash flow only by H1 FY27.
Middle East and West Asia disruption may hit export volumes; management said it is pushing domestic sales to compensate.
DGFT wheat flour export scheme is policy-dependent; management said it does not rely on it fully.
Several Q&A answers were inconsistent or incomplete, including the export order book, the margin split between B2B and B2C, and the retail gross margin figures.

544487|2026-06.headline: Patel Retail Q1 FY27 total income rose 69.35% YoY to INR310.24 crores, but EBITDA margin fell to about 6.3% on raw material intensity.
544487|2026-06.overview: Total income reached INR310.24 crores, up 69.35% YoY from INR183.19 crores, while EBITDA grew 23.92% to INR19.68 crores and PAT rose 37.43% to INR9.52 crores (EPS INR2.85). Management attributed the margin compression (about 133 bps decline cited, and a 233 bps figure also mentioned) to a higher raw-material-intensity mix in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked business amid volatile raw material prices and odd order timing. The company added stores at Rasayani and Babgaon in Q1 and opened its 53rd store at Uran (Raigad) after quarter-end, and expanded Indian Chaska into Madhya Pradesh. Management guided to positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 and 8 to 10 new stores in FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +69.35% YoY vs INR183.19 crores in Q1 FY26
decline of 133 bps as stated (233 bps also cited in same answer)

financial_highlights.value: around INR101 crores (as referenced by analyst)

financial_highlights.metric: Private label contribution to retail sales

segments.name: Retail (Patel R-Mart)
segments.commentary: 53 stores after Uran opening; average monthly sales per store put at INR80 lakh to INR1 crore, mature-store sales about INR20,000 per sq ft; ticket size INR500 to INR1,000; wastage below 0.1%. Payback about 24 months.

segments.name: Manufacturing / food processing
segments.commentary: Utilisation currently 50% to 55%, targeted at around 80% to 82% by FY27-FY28; automation expected to cut labour cost and improve quality consistency. Private label share of domestic sales cited at 45%, export sales at 37%.

segments.name: Exports and B2B
segments.commentary: Management stated about 40% of revenue from exports and rest from manufacturing and retail; export contribution to bottom line cited as 35% to 40%. These figures were not reconciled in the call.

segments.commentary: Expanded to Madhya Pradesh in August 2026, taking presence to eight states and one union territory; MP averaging INR10 lakh to INR12 lakh per month; whole spices category to be added this quarter.

segments.name: Online / quick commerce
segments.commentary: App has more than 50,000 downloads but online sales were around INR50 lakh in Q1; private label not yet listed on Blinkit or Zepto, with per-SKU terms being finalised; pilot quick commerce running from first stores.

segments.name: Apparel and fashion (general merchandise)
segments.commentary: 8% to 9% of revenue; inventory holding period 15 to 20 days.

qa_highlights.question: What must improve to move EBITDA margin from about 6.3% back to 8% to 9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 decline was due to higher raw material intensity in manufacturing, export and commodity-linked mix and volatile raw material prices; it expects improvement in coming quarters and not treating Q1 as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: Positive operating cash flow by H1 FY27 still on track, and working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Q1 balance sheet and cash flow not yet published; expects much better operating cash flow by H1, converting FY26 current-asset build into cash.

qa_highlights.question: How many new stores in FY27 and revenue contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: 8 to 10 stores by FY27, expected to contribute around INR1 crore per month in revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation and target?
qa_highlights.answer: Current utilisation 50% to 55%; targeted around 80% to 82% in the medium term, by end-FY27 to FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Share of own brands across channels?
qa_highlights.answer: Own brands about 17.5% of overall revenue; private label 17.55% of retail sales, 37% of export sales and 45% of domestic sales as stated by the CFO.

qa_highlights.question: Performance of recently opened stores vs older stores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new stores are operationally breakeven since day one, with some growing strongly; payback target about 24 months.

Online and quick commerce traction remains small (about INR50 lakh in Q1) and competition from platform in-house brands noted by analysts.

544487|2026-09.headline: Patel Retail Q2 FY27 income rose 33.5% to INR300.9 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 6.8% from 8.6% and PAT declined to INR9.9 crore.
544487|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 total income grew 33.5% YoY to INR300.9 crore while EBITDA rose 5.2% to INR20.5 crore and PAT fell to INR9.9 crore from INR10.1 crore. H1 FY27 income rose 49.6% to INR611.1 crore, with EBITDA up 13.6% to INR40.2 crore and PAT up 13.9% to INR19.4 crore, but margins compressed on higher COGS. Operating cash flow turned positive at INR31 crore in H1 FY27 against negative INR83.4 crore in FY26, and current borrowings fell to INR89.3 crore. Management guided to 8-10 new stores a year and said Q3 and Q4 margins should improve.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the operating cash flow swing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the swing mainly to recovering about INR29 crore or more from debtors in six months, plus better working capital rotation; inventory turns more than 4-5 times a year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the decline reflects 12-15 recently opened stores not yet mature, and expects them to mature within about six months.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Indian Chaska is at an early stage, did not disclose revenue targets, and expects more SKUs beyond the spices range.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall from 8.67% to 6.58% and what is sustainable?

544488|2026-03.headline: Vikram Solar FY26 revenue hit a record INR4,800 crore (+40% YoY) with EBITDA margin up to 19%, but guided FY27 non-DCR per-watt EBITDA lower at INR1.75–2.
544488|2026-03.overview: FY26 set records on revenue (INR4,800 crore), volumes (3.3 GW, +76%), EBITDA (INR917 crore, 19% margin) and PAT (INR470 crore, 10% margin), with Q4 revenue of INR1,450 crore and first 1 GW quarterly run rate. Management said Q4 per-watt cost rose INR0.80 against a INR0.60 realisation gain, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35. The order book stood at 8.2 GW at 31 March 2026, with distribution orders removed from the book and C&I DCR orders under renegotiation. The company announced a 6 GW wafer-ingot phase at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29) and a 15 GWh BESS target by FY30, while the 9 GW TOPCon cell plant has been pushed to a phased commissioning through Q4 FY27 and ramp in Q2 FY28.

segments.commentary: No captive cell capacity yet; 9 GW TOPCon Plus cell plant at Gangaikondan targets first cell December 2026 and completion of phases through March 2027, with a further 3 GW in FY28. A 2 GW DCR cell procurement agreement with Jupiter International supports FY27 DCR offtake, weighted to H2.

Gangaikondan 6 GW module plant in final stretch, first output on track for June 2026; Vallam 5 GW built in under nine months.

Wafer-ingot phase 1 of 6 GW at Gangaikondan (about INR3,700 crore, commissioning FY29; Q&A said March 2028), with advances of under INR100 crore in FY27; BESS cell construction from October 2026 over 24 months, FY27 land and initial spend under INR200 crore.
Management expects standard utilisation of 65–70% on modules and 70–75% on cells, on nameplate basis.
Capex to be funded through a mix of debt and equity, and internal accruals; the company expects to fund FY27 BESS and wafer-ingot outflows largely from internal accruals.
demand_pricing: India added 45 GW of solar in FY26 (against a 24 GW target, about 87% above FY25); cumulative base 150 GW. Utility-scale additions were a record 34 GW and rooftop 8.5 GW.

Management sees over 80 GW of grandfathered Non-DCR demand over two years, about 28 GW of live utility-scale DCR tenders and about 25 GW of inherent DCR demand from C&I, KUSUM and rooftop. Management expects DCR demand of 20–25 GW in FY27.

Cell costs rose during FY26 on higher silver prices and removal of China's export VAT rebate. Aluminium rose from $3,100 to $3,600 per ton; EVA cost rose with crude; partly offset by lower cell prices.
Approximately 80% of the order book has cell price pass-through clauses; FY26 per-watt overhead fell 16%.
Q4 realisations rose about INR0.60 per watt-peak while cost rose INR0.80, compressing per-watt EBITDA to about INR2.35 (DCR mandate from June 2026).

Distribution order book (about 1 GW) was removed from the 1.9 GW Q4 order inflow and moved to spot buying; distribution network about 110+ distributors and 550+ dealers/SIs. A US export project of about 0.6 GW was dropped after the IPP found it unviable.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the 1 GW distribution order book removed, and does the 1.9 GW order inflow include distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said inflow excludes distribution; the recurring distributor order book moved to spot buying as volumes shift to DCR and outsourced cell supply. Distribution was about 20% of Non-DCR volumes last year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA per watt-peak in Q4 and in the non-DCR business?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 per-watt EBITDA was about INR2.35, with non-DCR volumes guided at INR1.75–2 on average for FY27 and about INR5 for FY28 post cell integration (current about INR6).

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume and order plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 8 GW of production in FY27 (2 GW DCR, 6 GW non-DCR) against 8.2 GW order book at March 2026, of which 6 GW goes out in FY27 leaving 1.2 GW, with the rest to be won from the 87 GW grandfathered Non-DCR pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt trajectory and interest outflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Closing FY27 debt guided at about INR3,200 crore and FY28 at INR6,500–6,600 crore; interest on construction projects is capitalised until commissioning, so P&L impact is deferred.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company handling the US export orders and where would it source cells?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said exports to the US have slowed to near zero since November; about 1 GW of export orders are with long-standing IPPs and are being executed via cells sourced from North Africa, with EU, Australia and Middle East also explored.

qa_highlights.question: How are silver and silicon cost increases passed on to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: MSAs allow pass-through of cell cost and dollar appreciation to the extent of about 80% of the order book; future pass-through depends on the market once cell and wafer-ingot capacity comes in.

risks_watch: Per-watt EBITDA compression: Q4 cost rose INR0.80 vs realisation gain INR0.60, and FY27 non-DCR guidance is INR1.75–2, well below FY26 levels.

Execution risk on 9 GW cell plant (first cell targeted end-December 2026, ramp Q2 FY28) and 6 GW Gangaikondan module plant (June 2026); a sizable part of FY27 volume relies on a third-party 2 GW DCR cell supply.
Order book quality: about 1 GW distribution orders removed, C&I DCR orders under renegotiation, and US export order risk.
Rising interest and working capital needs with Vallam inventory; debt guardrails (DSCR above 2.5, net debt/equity below 1.5) and the INR6,500–6,600 crore FY28 debt level.
Raw material and silver cost pass-through (about 80% of order book) and cell price competition from domestic capacity additions.

544488|2026-06.headline: Vikram Solar Q1 FY27: record 1,006 MW volume (+32% YoY) and revenue ~INR1,563 cr, but EBITDA fell to INR126 cr (8.06% margin) as costs outran pass-through.

544495|2026-06.headline: NIS Management Q1 FY27 consolidated income rose 15.68% YoY to INR115.44 crore, with EBITDA up 36.24% to INR9.22 crore at a 7.99% margin.

Net profit was INR6.40 crore (up 35% YoY, margin 5.54%), while EPS of INR3.23 grew only 3.53%. Management reiterated the INR500 crore FY27 revenue goal, flagged that the CCTV segment posted a Q1 loss due to project timing, and declined to commit to a margin expansion path beyond 1-2% over two years. Net debt, the share price fall since IPO, and buyback ideas drew pointed investor questions that management largely deflected toward growth investment.

segments.commentary: Q1 revenue nil (INR0 lakh); net loss about INR57 lakh across the LLP and Keertika Academy.

The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

Management said margins were held broadly flat year-on-year, though Q4 margin was about 12% versus roughly 14% for the half year, which management attributed to a delayed MAHAGENCO order and related site disruption. Growth drivers were RDSS-funded transmission and distribution work and solar EPC, plus a INR640 crore (incl. 18% GST, about INR540 crore ex-GST) SCADA order from Konkan Railway. Receivables and retention balances rose, and management flagged 40% of FY26 sales coming in Q4 as a key working-capital issue.

544501|2026-09.headline: Sugs Lloyd H1 FY27 revenue rose 73% to INR213.31 crore and PAT 69% to INR20.01 crore, with order book at INR1,067 crore.

Q2 new orders totalled INR395 crore excluding GST, all from outside Bihar, which cut Bihar's share of the order book from about 82% to about 55%. segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Balance of H1 revenue. Amritsar solar plant scheduled for completion by December 2026. Management says EPC is becoming more competitive and it is shifting toward capex-plus-RESCO models through Sugs Renewables.

segments.commentary: Company says it holds more than half the domestic fault passage indicator market. Compact FPI completed testing and first unit to be supplied within the quarter. Target of about 10% of total revenue by FY28, covering all products together.

544502|2026-03.headline: FY26 revenue INR288 crore (up ~5%), EBITDA INR63 crore at ~22% margin, PAT up 42%; SteriPort capacity expansion targeted operational by 20 June 2026.
544502|2026-03.overview: Management reported FY26 revenue of INR288 crore, up about 5%, with EBITDA of INR63 crore at a stable ~22% margin and PAT up over 42% YoY, driven mainly by lower finance cost. Q4 FY26 revenue was about INR77 crore (up 6.8% on the stated basis) and Q4 PAT was INR5.5 crore, up 28% YoY. The SteriPort ISBM capacity expansion (6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year) is not yet contributing and is guided to start by 20 June 2026. Management guided to 24-25% blended EBITDA margin going forward, with SteriPort at ~27%, and said polymer cost increases of 60-70% are being passed through with a ~INR2 per bottle impact.

6.8% growth as stated on a YoY basis
management expects to fall by about half to INR10-12 crore, per analyst's question; not disputed

financial_highlights.change: Bajaj Finance refinancing done early April
expected to fall to single digit

segments.name: SVP (small volume parenterals)
segments.commentary: Inhalation solutions and preservative-free ophthalmics are ~20% of SVP revenue in FY26. New SVP line expected commissioning in October-December 2026; ophthalmic and inhalation products targeted for commercialisation in FY27-28.
