segments.commentary: Among the smallest SBUs; 70-80% of its revenue comes from the UK. Growth is product-development led (preservative-free classic pack in development), not capex-led.

guidance_outlook: SteriPort expansion expected to be operational by 20 June 2026 (stage-2 trial ~5 June, validation ~15 days); management kept a ~10-day buffer.
Management expects three full quarters of SteriPort contribution in FY27, with ~INR80-85 crore incremental revenue in year one.
Blended EBITDA margin expected at 24-25% going forward (existing ~22%, SteriPort ~27%); management described 25%+ as achievable once new capacity is sold out.
PAT margin of 5-6% seen as sustainable short term; expected to improve by at least 3% once operating leverage is fully realised, with PAT growing faster than EBITDA and sales.
Solar project (10.8 MW captive) expected to save ~INR75 lakh per month from about 25-30 May 2026 (per management's cost-saving view).
Plan to refinance a further INR30-40 crore of debt at lower rates within six months.
capex_capacity: SteriPort ISBM capacity being expanded from 6.6 crore to ~12 crore bottles per year; all equipment installed, stage-wise commissioning and Italian-engineer trials complete; mopping-up ongoing.

Management expects to run at 95-100% of the new capacity from day one, assuming 20 operating hours versus 24 for BFS; separately, an analyst's question on 90-92% utilisation was answered affirmatively in the call.
Inventory build expected in the first quarter after expansion; equilibrium in three to four months, with a 9-10 month cycle to normalise inventory.
New SVP line expected commissioning in October-December 2026.
State FDA plant-plan approval already obtained for SteriPort Line 3; state inspection expected to take about one week after full commissioning, running in parallel with validation.
demand_pricing: Polymer (PE/PP) input prices up roughly 60-70%; impact estimated at INR1.25-1.75 per container, or about INR2 per SteriPort bottle; management said selling prices have been revised and it expects to be broadly neutral, with the price correction slightly above cost increase because packaging, films and transport costs are also rising.
Price revision initiated about 20-25 days before the call with no customer resistance reported; for a 100 ml container the price increase is about 5.5-6% of selling price.

Management said power costs have fallen because of solar, and that polymer price pass-through typically lags, with price cuts on reversal expected to be partial (e.g., INR2 rise may reverse by INR0.75-1).

Indian IV fluid demand growing 8-10% YoY, ~INR185 crore market per management's estimate; two-port segment expected to grow 12-13%. SteriPort demand estimated at 20-25 crore bottles, rising to 75-80 crore bottles by 2030; management targets 20-25% share.
Export order visibility is about three to six months; East Africa purchases concentrated in September-March; no order book spanning a year.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company managing raw material price and supply pressure, and will gross margins be affected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management holds a four-month polymer buffer (up from three), sources mainly from South Korea, and says it has passed on the cost increase; it said gross margin should be unaffected, and the benefit of lower-cost inventory is expected in Q1 FY27 rather than Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Will hospitals downgrade from SteriPort to cheaper products given price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR2 per-bottle increase is immaterial given nursing-home charges of INR500-1,500 per bottle administered, and that no price resistance has been seen; it cited no compliance-related customer audit requirement for SteriPort beyond state FDA plan approval.

qa_highlights.question: What is the finance cost outlook and debt reduction plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About 90% of borrowings are now in single-digit interest; CRISIL rating improved one notch to BBB; management expects to replace INR30-40 crore more debt at lower rates in six months and to repay debt from cash flows; total debt INR234 crore at March 2026 fell to INR204 crore as of the call.

qa_highlights.question: What incremental revenue and margin should be expected from SteriPort in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed ~INR80-85 crore incremental revenue in FY27 from three quarters of operation (versus ~INR110-120 crore full year), and ~26-27% EBITDA margin for SteriPort.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital and receivables outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle is 120-125 days, targeted to ~110 days; receivables improved as old government and export dues were recovered and customers paid early ahead of price increases.

qa_highlights.question: What is the export share and top markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Exports were ~39% of FY26 revenue versus 32% in FY25; top markets include Thailand, UK, Philippines and South Sudan, with products marketed in 25-30 countries.

risks_watch: Commissioning slippage: SteriPort operational date of 20 June 2026 depends on stage-2 trials, validation and state FDA inspection.
Inventory build and ramp-up after expansion could pressure pricing and working capital in the first two to three quarters.
Polymer prices are volatile; management expects a lagged and partial price reversal, which could hurt margins as inventory is re-priced.
Competition in two-port systems (e.g., Eurohead-type products from other companies); management said these must demonstrate collapsibility to get the same NPPA pricing.
Contract structures with hospital chains are one-sided, and the company does not sign long-term contracts; order visibility is only three to six months.
Company declined to give the split of domestic sales between large hospital chains and standalone hospitals; a quantified order visibility figure for next quarter was promised later.

544502|2026-06.headline: Amanta Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~5% YoY to INR69 crore at ~22% EBITDA margin; SteriPort Line 3 commercial start slipped to late August.

SteriPort Line 3 slipped from Q1 to Q2 FY27 due to civil construction delays; management now targets commercial production in the last week of August after FDA plan approval and an inspection scheduled for August 21. The SVP facility is now guided to commercialise around March 2027 (FAT in the US in November). 544502|2026-09.headline: Amanta Q2 FY27 revenue rose 17% YoY to INR83.1 crore with EBITDA margin of 21.6%; SteriPort Line 3 commissioned, taking capacity to about INR11.6 crore.
544502|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR83.1 crore, up 17% YoY, with EBITDA up about 22% to INR18 crore at a 21.6% margin and PAT of INR4.86 crore, up 26%. H1 FY27 revenue was INR151.9 crore (up 12%), EBITDA INR33 crore (up 8%) and PAT INR8.17 crore (up 12%). SteriPort Line 3 was commissioned in early September 2026, and management reiterated FY27 revenue of INR420-430 crore on an annualised run-rate basis. Polymer price volatility was absorbed in the quarter, with price increases of about 4-4.5% taken across products; the SVP expansion has slipped from Feb-Mar 2027 to a Q1 FY28 start.

financial_highlights.value: about INR190 crore incl. about INR45 crore working capital

segments.name: SteriPort (2-port ISBM IV fluid)
segments.commentary: Capacity raised about 75% from INR6.6 crore to about INR11.6 crore per year with Line 3 at Kheda; Line 3 was running at about 55% in early November and management expects full utilisation from 20 November. Line 3 is expected to contribute about INR60 crore of revenue in FY27, with the INR110 crore annual run-rate guidance dependent on optimal utilisation.

segments.name: Small volume parenterals (SVP)
segments.commentary: SBU revenue is about INR55-65 crore; capacity to rise about 52% from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore in Q1 FY28, dedicated mainly to inhalation (BFS) and preservative-free ophthalmics. Management is targeting INR16 crore of SVP revenue in FY28 as a conservative figure, with a wider INR35-60 crore range cited as speculative.

segments.commentary: Management said contract and licensing revenue is about 2-3% of revenue, roughly INR25-30 crore for the year. International revenue was about 32% of Q2 FY27 revenue.

Power savings from the 10.8 MW captive solar plant estimated at about INR9 crore per year.

Management expects NPPA/NLEM distribution-margin reforms to hit hospital retail margins rather than manufacturer margins.

qa_highlights.question: What is current plant utilisation and target for FY27?

qa_highlights.question: Why did gross margin fall while EBITDA held steady?

qa_highlights.question: What is the current net debt and repayment plan?

qa_highlights.question: Will FY28 include SVP contribution and how much?

SteriPort is primarily India-centric activity, and SVP capacity that we are creating, right now inhalation products are made on one line.
And gain, it is very -- I would say it is very speculative to give number at this stage because, for one, the utilization is going to be very, very low.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management expects gross margin and product-mix benefits in Q3 and Q4 FY27 and polymer normalisation in 3-6 months, against a 21.6% Q2 EBITDA margin and 2-year aim of 25%-plus.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: SteriPort Line 3 already commissioned (capacity to about INR11.6 crore, up 75%) and ramping to full use from 20 Nov; SVP capacity from INR20.9 crore to about INR31 crore (52%) commissioning by end-March 2027 with revenue from Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Plant utilisation at 95-97% with Line 3 at about 55% ramping to full, expected to add about INR60 crore of SteriPort revenue in FY27 and FY27 guidance of INR420-430 crore annualised versus H1 run-rate of INR151.9 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management sees no near-term SteriPort capex given 12 crore plus 6 crore legacy capacity, with only INR7-20 crore product-development and automation items; yet 95-97% utilisation keeps a later glass-line idea open.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR420-430 crore annualised with Q3 and Q4 at Q2 run-rate (about INR83 crore a quarter), and Line 3 ramp could beat the INR60 crore FY27 contribution, but SVP upside is called speculative.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Polymer costs rose more than 70% at one point and are volatile, SVP has already slipped about 5 months, and Line 3 ramp to full use is only targeted from 20 Nov at about 55% now.

rows.label: New product launch

rows.label: Polymer cost normalisation and price pass-through
rows.why: Management expects polymer prices to normalise in 3-6 months and price rises of about 4-4.5% were taken, so margin could expand if oil-linked costs fall further, but this depends on oil.

rows.label: Debt reduction to about INR175-180 crore total by end FY27
rows.why: Total borrowings about INR190 crore in Sep 2026 with annual repayment of about INR30-35 crore, so debt falls as cash flow covers repayments.

rows.label: NPPA/NLEM distribution-margin reforms
rows.why: Management expects reforms to hit hospital retail margins rather than manufacturer margins, but the impact on SteriPort's premium hospital channel is not quantified.

544511|2026-03.headline: Karbonsteel crossed ₹300 crore revenue in FY26 with 10.86% EBITDA margin and ₹10.51 crore PAT, which management says normalises to ₹16.56 crore.
544511|2026-03.overview: FY26 revenue crossed ₹300 crore, but the company missed its ₹340 crore ideal level because of Khopoli exit, labour migration after the March LPG force majeure, and a ~₹40 crore shortfall from low-value labour jobs. Reported EBITDA margin was 10.86% and PAT ₹10.51 crore, including a ₹1.65 crore NCLT bad-debt write-off, ₹2.4 crore rent for the delayed Umargam expansion and Khopoli shifting costs. Order book was stated at about ₹350 crore as of May, up from near ₹200 crore. The Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes slipped from March to October 2026.

segments.name: Heavy and precision structural fabrication
segments.commentary: Core business; 70-80% of FY26 tonnage was complex custom work. Realisation about ₹100/kg for full fabrication versus ~₹30/kg for labour-only jobs; conversion margin ₹30-45/kg.

segments.name: PEB
segments.commentary: Revenue contribution fell to 0%; management says it will remain a small part as the company focuses on production rather than erection.

segments.name: Railways / bullet train
segments.commentary: Bullet train work (4,500 tonnes) was largely booked in the prior year; FY26 contribution nominal. Railway product development is at a very early stage.

guidance_outlook: Normalised EBITDA margin of 12-13% expected going forward; H2 FY26 normalised EBITDA cited at ~14%.
Production target ~40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation guided at 80-90%.
PAT margin ~4-5% for FY26 and above 5% for FY27; aspiration of 7-8% later.
Finance costs guided at ~4% of turnover in FY26; FY27 targeted revenue ₹400 crore with order book of at least ₹500 crore.
Automation expected to add 15-20% efficiency; automation alone contributes ~1% EBITDA margin uplift by FY28.
Long-term aspiration of ₹800-1,000 crore revenue and 7,000-8,000 tonnes per month, requiring post-FY27 expansion funded by internal accruals and equity.
Labour expected to return by end-June 2026; ~₹150 crore order pipeline expected around September-October.
capex_capacity: Umargam expansion from 30,000 to 54,000 tonnes; completion revised to October (management cited 'October 2025' in places, which appears to be a transcription error given the call date of June 2026); initially targeted March.
₹21 crore work-in-progress on the expansion; another ₹10-15 crore capex planned next year, split between shed/building and automation.
Sheds 1 and 2 about 60% complete; a blasting machine under installation; automation planned in cutting, automatic beam welding and fit-up centre.
1 MW solar plant in two phases at ~₹3-3.5 crore, expected online October-November; expected to cut power bills by over 50%. Energy cost ~₹25-30 lakh per month.
Khopoli facility (2.5 acres, rented) exited, removing ~5,000-6,000 tonnes of capacity; team consolidated at Umargam (20+ acres).
demand_pricing: Order book grew from ~₹200 crore to ~₹350 crore as of May; management targets at least ₹500 crore of orders against a ₹400 crore revenue target.
90-95% of orders are repeat business; clients include ArcelorMittal, a major Maharashtra steel company, two large business houses and a power company.
MOU signed for 15,000 tonnes specifically for data centres.
Steel prices rose from ₹50-55/kg to ₹65-70/kg; price variation clauses pass through most steel cost, but conversion and transport fixed portions are being accepted gradually.
Management says PEB peers realise ₹115-120/kg but are EPC contractors; not comparable as Karbonsteel only manufactures.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the EBITDA margin rise only 1% by FY28 if one-offs disappear?
qa_highlights.answer: The 1% uplift is attributed to automation alone; other improvements are expected beyond that. Normalised margin expected at 12-13%.

qa_highlights.question: Expected production and utilisation after expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40,000 tonnes annually at ~₹100/kg; FY26 utilisation 80-90%. Full 54,000-tonne capacity targeted for the following year.

qa_highlights.question: Solar capex and savings?
qa_highlights.answer: ₹3-3.5 crore for the solar plant, cutting bills by over 50%; eventually 100% solar power. Automation like laser cutting deferred until solar is in place due to power intensity.

qa_highlights.question: Will the labour issue be resolved?
qa_highlights.answer: Labour is returning; normalisation expected by end-June. April-May utilisation affected, Q1 utilisation about 80%.

Labour availability: migration after the March LPG crisis; normalisation hoped for end-June.
Single LPG supplier force majeure exposed supply risk; management now says multiple gas sources are available.
Steel and input-cost volatility; fixed conversion and transport costs not fully passed through.
Large rental and depreciation costs until new capacity is commissioned; finance cost ~₹15 crore vs. stated ~4% of turnover guidance.
Margin targets (12-13% normalised EBITDA; 7-8% PAT aspiration) well above reported 10.86% and ~3.5% PAT.

544512|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 106.5% YoY to INR725.6 crore and FY26 PAT rose 89% to INR115.5 crore, with working capital absorbing cash.
544512|2026-03.overview: Shringar reported Q4 FY26 revenue of INR725.6 crore (+106.5% YoY) with PAT of INR34 crore (+123.5%), and FY26 revenue of INR2,245.8 crore (+57.1%) and PAT of INR115.5 crore (+89%). Production capacity was raised from 2,500 kg to 4,000 kg in Q4, with FY26 utilisation at 87% on a blended 2,625 kg. The company entered bridal jewellery with Tanishq and Malabar Gold and Diamonds, and management reiterated about 30% value CAGR guidance for the next two to three years. Management acknowledged that working capital growth absorbed cash, leaving free cash flow negative, and said it expects to shift toward outright sales and organised clients within about two quarters.

segments.commentary: About 70% of FY26 revenue from outright sales and 30% from job work per management; mangalsutra sales are guided up 33-35% within FY27. Corporate clients were 49% and non-corporate 51% of FY26 revenue.

segments.name: Job work
segments.commentary: Job work revenue (labour fee) was INR28 crore in FY26 versus INR26 crore in FY25, per management.

segments.name: Bridal jewellery
segments.commentary: Launched in Q4 FY26; first lot delivered in May 2026 to Titan (Tanishq). Management expects bridal to be about one-third of revenue within FY27 and on par with mangalsutra in about three years, though contribution is currently small.

guidance_outlook: Value growth guidance of about 30% CAGR over the next two to three years, stated as a minimum target; management said it could exceed 30-35% if gold prices stay steady.
FY27 mangalsutra sales expected to rise about 33-35% within the year.
Volume growth of about 15% in FY26; management aims to sustain this and accelerate toward 30-35% if gold prices stay steady.

Installed capacity stays at 4,000 kg for FY27, with further ramp-up expected in coming quarters.

Gold hedging: about 3.5 tonnes annual production; 30% barter (gold-to-gold, already hedged), 17% GML, 13% MCX hedged, roughly 60% hedge ratio.
Around 10 large exhibitions organised in the year, which raised advertising spend.
demand_pricing: Client base of 1,333 customers across India and abroad; management plans to shift weight toward organised players such as Tata, Birla, Reliance, Malabar, Joyalukkas, Kalyan and PNG.
Malabar Gold and Diamonds accounted for 17% of revenue; Titan is a job-work client, so management said its value is not comparable.
Average inventory cost of gold about INR10,500 per gram on weighted-average basis; management cited gold prices up nearly 2x YoY (INR1,52,228 as of 15 April 2026).
Management said April and May 2026 were not particularly difficult, with corporate orders continuing without interruption.
Gold import duty raised from 6% to 15%; management said the increase is absorbed into domestic gold prices and has not caused distinct difficulties.
Management cited about 1 crore weddings in FY26 and weddings growing about 7-8% annually.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the working capital increase and the debt position?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the debt-equity ratio is 0.27 and inventory churn is about five times; higher working capital was needed to support revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sharp rise in other expenses in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it mainly to notional hedging losses on MCX-hedged gold, plus about 10 exhibitions, machinery and setup costs for the new factory, and higher CSR spend.

qa_highlights.question: What is the job work versus outright sales split and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Roughly 30% job work and 70% outright sales. Job work earned INR28 crore in FY26 as a labour fee. Management said converting job work to outright sales could lift revenue to INR70-80 crore on the same volume and triple profit on that volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did working capital rise and was the cycle lengthening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said outright sales require more capital, which is the trade-off for higher margin. It expects organised clients with fixed payment dates to ease cash-flow churn over time. It did not give debtor or inventory day figures.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 30% guidance value or volume growth, and does it include bridal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 30% guidance is value growth and a minimum target. Bridal is not included in that guidance; it could push growth above 30% if bridal reaches parity with mangalsutra within three years.

qa_highlights.question: When will free cash flow turn positive?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it expects to convert a significant portion of operations to outright contracts within about two quarters, which should help move cash flow from negative to positive.

risks_watch: Negative free cash flow in Q4 FY26 driven by working capital; watch debtor and inventory days and whether cash flow turns positive in about two quarters.
Gold price volatility (near doubling YoY) and hedging losses; FY26 hedge ratio about 60%.
Shift from job work to outright sales raises capital needs and inventory risk, and depends on clients such as Tanishq converting contracts.
Q4 EBITDA margin fell 41 bps YoY despite higher gross margin, driven by hedging notional losses, exhibitions and CSR spend.
Bridal jewellery is at an early stage with a small contribution; the first lot was delivered in May 2026.
Management did not give a split of revenue by client beyond Malabar at 17%; client concentration remains unclear.

544515|2026-06.headline: Urban Company Q1 FY27 consolidated NTV rose 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore; Services NTV grew 29% and InstaHelp loss narrowed to ₹(132) crore.
544515|2026-06.overview: Consolidated NTV grew 42% YoY to ₹1,465 crore and revenue rose 44% to ₹528 crore, with orders up 79% YoY to 13.2 million. Core Services NTV accelerated for a fourth straight quarter to 29% growth (₹1,056 crore), and Services adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 6.9% of NTV. Consolidated loss was ₹(65) crore, almost entirely from InstaHelp, while the rest of the business delivered an adjusted EBITDA of ₹67 crore. Management retained its guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31, and framed InstaHelp as the main investment area.

financial_highlights.change: +5.2 pp YoY (stated as 170 bps improvement in the margin line in the Q&A)
improved from (11.4)% a year ago (410 bps)

1.2 million new customers added in the quarter

segments.name: Core Services
segments.commentary: NTV ₹1,056 crore, growing 29% YoY, the fourth consecutive quarter of acceleration (10%→19%→21%→26%→29%). Adjusted EBITDA margin 6.9% of NTV, up 5.2 pp YoY per the call; management says the 29% base was muted by unseasonal rains and monsoon in the prior year.

segments.name: International
segments.commentary: NTV ₹237 crore, up 76% YoY (58% ex-currency). UAE and Singapore both grew strongly; the Saudi Arabia JV is approaching profitability. UAE and Saudi JV are described as nearing or at profitability, and the company is not planning new international markets.

segments.commentary: NTV ₹119 crore (+51% YoY), net revenue ₹95 crore (+60% YoY); adjusted EBITDA loss ₹(132) crore, or (7.3)% of NTV versus (11.4)% a year ago. Largest investment; management expects it to need 2 or more years of investment and aims for adjusted breakeven within about 18 months.

guidance_outlook: Retains guidance of consolidated adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28.
Retains guidance of ₹1,000 crore adjusted EBITDA by FY31.
Long-term Services adjusted EBITDA margin guidance of 9-10% of NTV; currently at 6.9%. Management said it is not in a rush and sees the target as achievable without trading off growth.
Management said Services will be a cash-generating business going forward and that it intends to keep it profitable; InstaHelp is expected to need 2 years or more of investment.
Management explicitly declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29% trend, saying the company does not want to set the wrong expectations.
Top-15-city TAM for InstaHelp is ₹7,000-12,000 crore NTV annually; management's base case is ₹7,000-8,000 crore and the bull case is ₹10,000-12,000 crore.

Core Services trainer and infrastructure capacity is being scaled up with AI support; management says the company is 'all hands on deck' as supply grows.
Beauty segment: partners are being retrained and retooled, and the company moved to a majority of professionals having access to two-wheelers, with the target of approaching 100%.

Services is expected to consume less capital as InstaHelp is scaled; management said capital allocation will be reviewed once InstaHelp approaches adjusted breakeven (hopefully within about 18 months).
demand_pricing: Management said Q1 was among the best quarters in the company's history, with growth broad-based.

InstaHelp pricing: sustainable professional payout is about ₹130-160 per hour, with ₹150 as the rule of thumb. Management said an AOV of about ₹300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even, with ₹200 per hour required to clear gross breakeven.

Management said competitors in the InstaHelp category have pricing of ₹80-120 per hour for full-month subscriptions and that competitive intensity is high; it said the company has no reason to comment on rival strategies.
Management said the 3 major players have limited their household coverage to about 3.5-4 million households; the company believes most spending goes to subsidised repeat orders.
Management said the company has 'underestimated' the Tier 2 opportunity, with Tier 2 cities performing as well as Tier 1.

Management said it is seeing acceleration in MAUs, DAUs and MTUs, with conversion rates improving; the marketing spend in Services was about ₹25 crore in the quarter versus ₹24 crore a year ago (flat).

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: is the Cheaper, Faster, Better flywheel now visible enough to call a bold trajectory shift in Services NTV growth, and can growth be guided higher?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the flywheel comes from densifying many micro-markets, which improves partner utilisation, lowers churn and supports trust. It cited UC Instant (30-60 minute service) as a new driver. It declined to give growth guidance, said the 29% was helped by a muted prior-year base from unseasonal rains and monsoon, and said the margin of 6.9% is in line with the 9-10% long-term target, which is not a trade-off against growth.

qa_highlights.question: Morgan Stanley: why should InstaHelp get capital and attention, and how will capital be allocated over two years between Services, new segments and international?
qa_highlights.answer: InstaHelp is strategically relevant because its high frequency keeps users on the app weekly. Services is to be profitable and cash generating; UAE and Singapore are profitable wholly owned subsidiaries; the Saudi JV is nearing profitability. InstaHelp needs two years or more of investment, with capital allocation revisited at adjusted breakeven, hopefully within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: why not export the UAE and Saudi model to new international markets, given Core Services is generating cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited bandwidth as the main constraint. It said playbooks need local customisation plus some luck, and that earlier Australia and US launches did not succeed. It will stay focused on UAE, Saudi Arabia and India, with no plans for new international markets for now.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: where does Services margin go from 6.9% of NTV versus the 9-10% target, and would the company cap margin around 10% or reinvest?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the goal is to reach the 9-10% range without rushing and without trading growth for margin. Priority one is growing fast, priority two is margin expansion. Once it reaches about 10%, it will decide whether to lift margins further or reinvest for faster growth.

qa_highlights.question: Goldman Sachs: is the InstaHelp TAM structurally lower, and would the company operate at a narrow loss if competition leaves room for only two players?
qa_highlights.answer: The base case is INR 7,000-8,000 crore NTV and the bull case is INR 10,000-12,000 crore, with 3 orders per user per month. Management said the 3 major players have limited coverage to about 3.5-4 million households and that subsidised repeat orders dominate spend. It expects a low single-digit market share outcome and says it will not spend heavily on the category to drive share, while being opinionated about winning micro-markets.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: what AOV is needed for InstaHelp to break even, and is there scope for growth above 29%?
qa_highlights.answer: Sustainable professional payout is INR 130-160 per hour, with INR 150 as the rule of thumb. Gross breakeven needs about INR 200 per hour, and an AOV of about INR 300 is needed for InstaHelp to break even. Management said breakeven could take a couple of years or up to 5 years, and it declined to give growth guidance beyond the 29%.

qa_highlights.question: Bank of America: how is AI being used and how much margin benefit is there?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 90-95% of the code is now written by AI, and that support, supply-side onboarding, quality audits and fraud detection are increasingly AI-led. Marketing and Finance/HR run AI end-to-end. It said the margin benefit has started to show but there is a long way to go.

qa_highlights.question: Kotak: is Beauty acceleration sustainable, and are the 30-40 annual transactions per user assumption and consolidation prospects realistic?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Beauty has seen a resurgence after retraining and retooling partners, and that the company had underinvested there a couple of years back. Two-wheeler access for Beauty professionals is now a majority. It expects 3 transactions per month, not 30-40, for the 10-12 lakh household case. It expects private players to keep burning cash and believes it will be the eventual winner in the category.

qa_highlights.question: Bellwether: what is driving the 5 lakh quarter-on-quarter user addition, what marketing spend is involved, and what training and capacity constraints exist in InstaHelp and Core Services?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the user growth is largely from MAU, DAU and MTU growth and better conversion, and that marketing spend in Services was about INR 25 crore versus INR 24 crore a year ago. For Core, it said capacity is comfortable but is being scaled up, with all hands on deck, to match trainer and infrastructure growth. It said InstaHelp supply is also being expanded.

qa_highlights.question: Emkay: is the shift to premium products a sign of a premium customer base, and will the company expand beyond water purifiers and smart locks?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its products, such as the M3 water purifier with a 3-year no-service, no-filter-change design, are aimed at lowering lifecycle cost. It said it is not building a durables company and will keep its focus on a small number of categories, mainly water purifiers and smart locks, with the aim of serving the top households in India.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said Native is on track for profitability, AC will be a disciplined build-up with R&D the bulk of losses, and any new category would take one to two quarters of learning before scale.

qa_highlights.question: Is professional supply or retention a rate limiter, and what is steady-state unit economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the challenge is retaining high-quality professionals, not sourcing. Experts care about net take-home pay; the company frames pricing and payouts as competitive. Steady-state unit economics remain under evaluation with a cited framework of payout ₹150 per hour, with ₹50 covering costs at best utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the acceleration in professional-services growth and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said professional growth of 16% is a leading indicator; drivers are utilisation, targeting, and onboarding. Management declined to give specific projections.

qa_highlights.question: Will Native offline distribution expand pan-India in modern retail?
qa_highlights.answer: Offline share is small and in a learning phase; modern retail response is good; management will expand calibrated and slowly.

risks_watch: Competitive intensity in Core Services and International; management says losses are a deliberate choice.
Average spend growth slowing to 3% versus historical 6–7%.
Professional partner retention and churn as supply expands.
Native profitability and AC device adoption, with a one-to-two-quarter learning phase before scale.
Use and deployment of the ₹2,500 crore fundraise and any M&A execution.
544515|2026-09.management_tone: Confident and assertive on growth, profitability trajectory and the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal, with management repeatedly calling Native's losses a deliberate choice. More guarded on specifics: declined to give partner-growth projections, did not quantify average-spend slowdown beyond mix and seasonality, and said the AC launch would be calibrated and slow.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core Services contribution margin rose 110 bps to 3.5% against a 9-10% target, international adjusted EBITDA margin improved 190 bps to 2% of NTV, and Native loss per order fell 19% QoQ to ₹279.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No physical capacity additions quantified; Native AC is app-limited in a 1-2 quarter learning phase and Native offline is being expanded slowly and calibrated, so no plant or line adds are signalled for the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides Q2+Q3 combined consolidated NTV growth of 50-55% after Q2 NTV rose 39.1% to ₹1,432.3 crore, with orders up 63% QoQ to 6.23 million and annual transacting customers up 34.5% to almost 10 million.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation figure disclosed and no capex guided, but the ₹2,500 crore fundraise for organic build-out and selective M&A creates a funding base that could lead to announcements; management said nothing imminent.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Orders rose 63% QoQ to 6.23 million, international NTV grew 66.2% and management guides Q2+Q3 combined consolidated growth of 50-55%, so upside exists if festive-season onboarding converts.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Average spend growth slowed to about 3% vs historical 6-7%, Insta Help faces a tougher base (Q2 growth 26.3%), and professional supply grew 16% vs NTV 26%, which could pressure the Q2+Q3 NTV growth target of 50-55%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Native AC device has launched (learning phase, app-limited) and M3 water purifier and Lock Ultra are in modern retail, with gold premium service set to scale across categories.

rows.label: Consolidated breakeven by Q3 FY28
rows.why: Management reiterated breakeven by Q3 FY28 and is confident of the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal, with Core Services adjusted EBITDA at ₹30 crore ex-investments and trailing-four-quarter ₹119 crore; the Native investment of ₹174 crore in Q2 is the main drag.

rows.label: International growth (UAE, Saudi, Singapore)
rows.why: International NTV grew 66.2% YoY with Q2+Q3 combined growth guided at 50-55%, and management says war-related concerns are behind it.

rows.label: ₹2,500 crore fundraise and M&A
rows.why: Fundraise of up to ₹2,500 crore is framed as flexibility for organic build-out and selective M&A, with cash and treasury of ₹1,901 crore already on the balance sheet and nothing imminent.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, the Q3 FY28 breakeven and the ₹1,000 crore FY31 goal, and framed Native's losses as deliberate; analysts pushed on the rationale for the ₹2,500 crore raise, the slowdown in average spend to about 3%, and professional supply, where management declined partner-growt
